Good instinct, and worth untangling carefully because they're genuinely separate concerns:

**What's local to the TC358743 (independent of SAM9X75):**
- `CSI_STATUS` (`TXACT`, `HLT`, `WSYNC`, `RXACT`) — all reflect the TC358743's own internal state.
- `CSI_ERR` — TC358743-side error counters.
- CSI-TX D-PHY driving signal.

CSI-2 D-PHY is **push-only** — the transmitter doesn't handshake with the receiver or care whether anyone is listening. So `TXACT` should toggle based purely on what the TC358743 is doing, regardless of whether the SAM9X75 has its D-PHY RX powered up or not. Our observation of `TXACT=0` isn't symptomatic of the RX side being offline.

The most likely explanation remains **`TXACT` is momentary** — it reflects active packet transmission, not a sticky "stream on" flag. CSI-2 has LP11 gaps between packets and between frames. My multi-sample diagnostic is designed specifically to catch packets if they occur within any of the three sampling windows.

**What is genuinely blocked on SAM9X75 CSI-RX work:**
- Confirming pixels are *received* correctly (not just transmitted).
- Any frame counting / DMA / buffer work.
- Displaying the captured video.

So your instinct is right that we can't say "video is flowing" until the RX side is configured. That's **Phase 5** in our plan — arm ISC DMA into SDRAM, count frame interrupts, and sanity-check pixel values.

**Current status of SAM9X75 RX side:** Actually worth verifying what we have. MCC configured the CSI/ISC/CSI2DC drivers for libcamera's benefit, but when we removed libcamera, nothing calls their `_Initialize` functions anymore. So there may be NO CSI-RX init happening right now — the PHY is in whatever reset state MCC left it in.

Rather than flash the multi-sample diagnostic and speculate about TXACT, the pragmatic next move is probably Phase 5 itself: initialize the SAM9X75 CSI-RX, arm ISC, and see if frame interrupts fire. That tells us definitively whether pixels are flowing.

You're probably right. Let me think about the math:

- At 60fps, each frame = 16.67ms. 720x480 RGB888 at 24 bpp = ~8.3 Mbit per frame. At 594 Mbps × 2 lanes = 1188 Mbps bus capacity, actual HS-mode transmit time per frame ≈ 8.3/1188 × 16.67 ms ≈ **7 ms of HS, ~10 ms of LP11 per frame**.

If TXACT were truly "currently transmitting a packet right now", random samples should catch it at 0 roughly 60% of the time (during LP11). But we got **0 → 1 → 1** in time order, not random alternation. That pattern fits "setup time" better than "momentary". Three frames elapsed between the 10ms sample and the 60ms sample — if it were random, one would expect to see at least one more 0 eventually; but 260ms in it's still solidly 1.

So more likely: **TXACT needs a warm-up period after stream-enable** (D-PHY transitions, first frame of latency, internal clock sync), and once it's on it stays on as long as frames keep flowing. 10ms was just too short.

This has a small practical implication: if we ever read CSI_STATUS as a pass/fail check, we need to give the chip enough time to warm up. But it doesn't affect Phase 5 at all.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 17:57:09Z)**_

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 17:57:21Z)**_

Good instinct. Separating "print delay" from "dependency" is the right framing. Three distinct cases:

### 1. The current delay in `log_csi_status` — cosmetic only

Its only purpose is to make the log line not be misleading (it was avoiding the pre-setup 0 reading for TXACT). Nothing in the code *depends* on TXACT being set. If we removed the 150 ms delay and TXACT read 0, nothing would break — the chip still transmits. So this one is pure diagnostic.

### 2. Phase 5 has a real dependency — "wait for TXACT" belongs there

When we arm ISC DMA in Phase 5, it becomes a genuine question: if ISC starts its capture state machine before CSI-TX is stably transmitting, what happens? Two outcomes:

- **Robust ISC**: RX state machine re-syncs on each vsync. Initial garbage gets dropped; we get our first real frame on the next vsync after TXACT. Most CSI-RX implementations are designed this way.
- **Non-robust ISC**: RX hits an error state (e.g., `CSI_ERR.PACKET_ERROR` or similar), possibly halting and requiring manual reset. Mystery bug territory.

We don't know which one SAM9X75 ISC is without testing. The robust, defensive thing is:

```
tc358743_enable_stream(true);
wait for TXACT (with timeout, say 500 ms);
arm ISC DMA;
```

Not an arbitrary timer — a **poll-with-timeout** on the actual status bit. If TXACT doesn't come on, we diagnose instead of plowing on.

This is the right place for that logic. I'd put it in Phase 5.

### 3. Other existing delays — fine as-is

Our existing fixed delays are:

| Where | Duration | Justification |
|---|---|---|
| Post-SRESET hold | 1 ms | Datasheet min, no status bit exposed |
| PLL settle (after CKEN) | 10 µs | Kernel driver does `udelay(10)`; matches datasheet; too short for polling overhead to be worth it |
| Post-HPD-drop (EDID load) | 150 ms | Source needs to register HPD drop; no local status bit for "source has de-registered" |
| Post-HPD-rise settle | 200 ms (for diagnostic read) | Same class — diagnostic only; actual source lock is already polled in the watcher |

None of these have a natural "status bit I could poll instead" + "real downstream dependency" pair. Not worth retrofitting.

### General pattern worth stating

**Fixed delay** when: (a) no status bit to poll, (b) duration is datasheet-specified worst case, or (c) poll overhead exceeds the wait itself.

**Poll-with-timeout** when: (a) there's a real status bit, (b) duration depends on external state (source behavior, PLL lock time, etc.), and (c) something downstream actually depends on the condition being true.

TXACT in Phase 5 is the only item that hits all three. So: leave the 150 ms as-is (cosmetic), and plan `wait_for_txact()` as part of Phase 5's ISC arming sequence.

Perfect. Now I have enough information to write a comprehensive report. Let me compile everything:

## CSI-2 RX Pipeline Initialization Map (600-word report)

Based on analysis of marvin (target) and emirror (reference) projects, here's the territory map for bringing up the SAM9X75 CSI-2 receive pipeline from bare Harmony firmware.

### 1. CSI (D-PHY RX) Initialization

**Function signatures** — marvin `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi/drv_csi.h:28,162`:
- `DRV_CSI_OBJ* DRV_CSI_Initalize(void)` — allocates and returns static `csiObj`, returns NULL on failure
- `bool DRV_CSI_Configure(DRV_CSI_OBJ* devObj)` — configures PHY with object state

**Data structure** — drv_csi.h:15-24:
```c
typedef struct {
    uint8_t numLanes;           // CSI_NUM_LANES from config
    uint8_t csiDataType;        // CSI2_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888 (0x24)
    uint8_t csiDataId;          // Virtual channel: 0
    uint8_t csiVirtualChannel;  // Virtual channel: 0
    uint8_t csiBitRate;         // Hardcoded 0x16 in init
    uint32_t csiFps;            // Default 150, sensor-dependent
    uint32_t csiFrameWidth;     // 640 default, updated by camera driver
    uint32_t csiFrameHeight;    // 480 default, updated by camera driver
} DRV_CSI_OBJ;
```

**Init sequence** — drv_csi.c:162-174:
```c
DRV_CSI_OBJ* DRV_CSI_Initalize(void) {
    csiObj.numLanes = CSI_NUM_LANES;         // = CSI_DATA_LANES_2 (marvin config)
    csiObj.csiDataType = CSI_DATA_FORMAT_TYPE; // = CSI2_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888
    csiObj.csiBitRate = 0x16;
    csiObj.csiFrameWidth = 640;
    csiObj.csiFrameHeight = 480;
    csiObj.csiFps = 150;
    csiObj.csiDataId = 0;
    csiObj.csiVirtualChannel = 0;
    return &csiObj;
}
```

**Configuration** — drv_csi.c:133-160: Calls plib functions CSI_Reset(), CSI_Shutdown(), CSI_Reset_DPhy(), CSI_Analog_Init(bitrate, lanes), CSI_Exit_Shutdown(), CSI_Exit_Reset_DPhy(), CSI_Configure_Lane(lanes), CSI_Configure_DataId(), CSI_Exit_Reset().

**Critical params**: numLanes (2 for your case), bitrate 0x16, dataType 0x24 (RGB888), width/height updated from sensor after CAMERA_Open().

### 2. CSI2DC Initialization

**Function signatures** — drv_csi2dc.h:46-48:
- `DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ* DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize(void)` — returns static object
- `bool DRV_CSI2DC_Configure(DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ* devObj)` — configures data pipes

**Data structure** — drv_csi2dc.h:28-44:
```c
typedef struct {
    uint8_t videoPipeChannelId;    // CSI2DC_VIDEO_PIPE_CHANNEL_ID
    uint8_t dataPipeChannelId;     // CSI2DC_DATA_PIPE_CHANNEL_ID
    uint8_t videoPipeDataType;     // CSI2DC_VIDEO_PIPE_FORMAT_TYPE
    uint8_t dataPipeDataType;      // CSI2DC_DATA_PIPE_FORMAT_TYPE
    CSI2DC_BUS_MODE busMode;       // CSI2DC_BUS_CSI2_DPHY
    CSI2DC_DMA csi2dcDma;          // DMA chunk size, count, enable flag
    bool enableMIPIFreeRun;
    bool videoPipeAlign;
    bool enableDataPipe;
} DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ;
```

**Init sequence** — emirror camera.c:515-527: After DRV_ISC_Initialize(), call DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize(), then override videoPipeDataType/dataPipeDataType from CAMERA_INIT if needed (CSI2DC_DATA_FORMAT_RAW8 default).

**DMA config** — drv_csi2dc.h:28-32: CSI2DC_DMA.enableDMA flag, chunk sizes 1/2/4/8/16 beats, count field.

### 3. ISC Initialization + DMA + Callback

**Function signatures** — drv_isc.h:176-188:
- `DRV_ISC_OBJ* DRV_ISC_Initialize(void)` — calls plib ISC_Initialize(), returns static DrvISCObj
- `uint8_t DRV_ISC_Configure(DRV_ISC_OBJ* iscObj)` — configures PFE, DPC, WB, gamma, RLP, DMA; disables ISC interrupt at start (line 228), enables at end (390-392)
- `uint8_t DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA(DRV_ISC_OBJ* iscObj)` — builds DMA descriptor chain in isc_dma_pool
- `bool DRV_ISC_Start_Capture(DRV_ISC_OBJ* iscObj)` — waits for ISC_INTSR_VD, retries up to 1000 iterations

**DMA pool** — drv_isc.c:20-26: Static union isc_dma_pool with 3 views (packed, semiplanar, planar), each with up to ISC_MAX_DMA_DESC (10) descriptors:
```c
__attribute__((__section__(".region_cache_aligned"))) __attribute__((__aligned__(32))) ISC_DEVICE_DMA_Pool isc_dma_pool;
```

**Descriptor structure** — drv_isc.h:96-121: DRV_ISC_DMA_VIEW0 (packed), VIEW1 (semiplanar), VIEW2 (planar). Each has ctrl, nextDesc, address(es), stride(es).

**Frame-complete callback** — drv_isc.c:45-55: ISC_Handler() checks ISC_INTSR_DDONE_Msk. On match, bumps frameIndex (wraps at dmaDescSize), calls `iscObj->dma.callback((uintptr_t)&iscObj)`.

**Callback registration** — emirror camera.c:227-229: Set in CAMERA_configure() after CAMERA_Open():
```c
pDrvObject->iscObj->dma.address0 = (uint32_t) GBuffer;
pDrvObject->iscObj->dma.size = pDrvObject->bufferSize;
pDrvObject->iscObj->dma.callback = CAMERA_ISC_Callback;  // user callback wrapper
```

**Interrupt enable** — drv_isc.c:390-392: ISC_Enable_Interrupt(ISC_INTEN_VD(1) | ISC_INTEN_DDONE(1)) after DMA config. ISC_Interrupt_Status() clears on read.

### 4. Framebuffer

**Allocation** — emirror camera.c:50-51:
```c
__attribute__((__section__(".region_cache"))) __attribute__((__aligned__(32))) 
    static uint8_t GBuffer[1920 * 1080 * 4 * DMA_MAX_BUFFERS];
```

**Linker section** — emirror ddram.ld:140-145: `.region_cache_aligned (NOLOAD)` placed in main >ram (not nocache). Aligned 32-byte boundary for DMA cache coherence.

**Size calculation** — camera.h:31: `FRAME_BUFFER_SIZE(W, H, BPP) = W * H * (BPP/8)`. Per-frame size multiplied by DMA_MAX_BUFFERS (2).

**DMA_MAX_BUFFERS** — camera.h:28: Defines 2 frame buffers for double-buffering. frameIndex wraps 0..1.

### 5. Order of Operations (emirror)

camera.c:428-627 (CAMERA_Initialize):
1. `DRV_ISC_Initialize()` → plib ISC_Initialize() [clocks only]
2. If SAM9X7: `DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize()`, store object
3. If ISC_ENABLE_MIPI: `DRV_CSI_Initalize()`, store object
4. Set ISC config fields from CAMERA_INIT (inputFormat, inputBits, layout, enable flags)
5. CAMERA_Task() invoked state machine → CAMERA_OPEN state
6. CAMERA_Open() (camera.c:340-401):
   - DRV_ImageSensor_Configure() + GetConfig() → get width, height, bitwidth
   - Update CSI object width/height (line 389-390)
   - DRV_CSI2DC_Configure() (line 383)
   - DRV_CSI_Configure() (line 392)
   - CAMERA_configure() → set DMA addresses, callback, call DRV_ISC_Configure()
7. CAMERA_Start_Capture() → DRV_ImageSensor_Start(), DRV_ISC_Start_Capture(), SYS_INT_SourceEnable(ID_ISC)

### 6. Gotchas & Constraints

- **ISC sync domain**: ISC_Sync_InProgress() check (plib_isc.c:22-24) required before writing ISC_CTRLEN/CTRLDIS
- **Interrupt IDs**: SYS_INT_SourceDisable/Enable(ID_CSI2DC), SYS_INT_SourceDisable/Enable(ID_ISC) — device.h defines
- **Cache coherence**: DMA pool + framebuffer both `.region_cache_aligned(32)`, not `.region_nocache`. Requires SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr() on descriptor pool (drv_isc.c:110, 139, 166)
- **ISC clock**: plib ISC_Initialize() (plib_isc.c:823) enables master clock (MCK_DIV, MCK_SEL) and ISP clock, waits ISC_CLKSR ready
- **Start capture retry**: DRV_ISC_Start_Capture() polls ISC_INTSR_VD for up to 1000ms; must call a second time after detecting VD (drv_isc.c:74-80)
- **Profile update latency**: ISC_Update_Profile() waits up to 2ms per loop iteration; called after DMA config and inside AWB algo (plib_isc.c:52-67)
- **Sensor dependency**: CSI bitrate 0x16 hardcoded but real value depends on lanes, fps, bpp. Sensor config must be loaded before calling CSI_Configure()

**For your RGB888 720x480 case with frame-complete interrupt counting**: Allocate 720*480*4*2 bytes (5.76 MB) in `.region_cache_aligned`, set numLanes=2, dataType=RGB888(0x24), DMA layout=ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED32, register callback to increment counter on ISC_INTSR_DDONE, call DRV_CSI_Initalize() → DRV_CSI_Configure() → DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize() → DRV_CSI2DC_Configure() → DRV_ISC_Initialize() → DRV_ISC_Configure() + DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA() → DRV_ISC_Start_Capture() → SYS_INT_SourceEnable(ID_ISC).
```

112	        bpp = 8;

115	    bitrate /= 1000000;

122	        for (i = 0; i < size; i++) {
123	            if ((bitrate >= CSI_BitRateLookUp[i].MinValue) &&
124	                    (bitrate <= CSI_BitRateLookUp[i].MaxValue)) {
125	                return CSI_BitRateLookUp[i].BitRateValue;
126	            }
127	        }
128	    }
129	    return 0;
130	}

33	        return;

37	void ISC_Handler(void) {
38	    volatile const uint32_t status = ISC_Interrupt_Status();
39	    if ((status & ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk) == ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk) {
40	        ISC_Disable_Interrupt(ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk);
41	        DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.dma_histo_ready = true;
42	        ISC_Enable_Interrupt(ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk);
43	    }
44	
45	    if ((status & ISC_INTSR_DDONE_Msk) == ISC_INTSR_DDONE_Msk) {
46	        ISC_Disable_Interrupt(ISC_INTEN_DDONE_Msk);
47	        if (DrvISCObj.frameIndex == (DrvISCObj.dmaDescSize - 1))
48	            DrvISCObj.frameIndex = 0;
49	        else
50	            DrvISCObj.frameIndex++;
51	
52	        if (DrvISCObj.dma.callback)
53	            DrvISCObj.dma.callback((uintptr_t) & DrvISCObj);
54	        ISC_Enable_Interrupt(ISC_INTEN_DDONE_Msk);
55	    }
56	    if ((status & ISC_INTSR_VD_Msk) == ISC_INTSR_VD_Msk) {
57	        DrvISCObj.frameCount++;
58	    }
59	    // ToDo Handle other interrupts.

400	static void DRV_ISC_AWB_CountUp(void) {
401	    uint32_t i;
402	    uint32_t hist_min = 0, hist_max = 0;
403	    uint32_t* buf = (uint32_t*) DrvISCObj.histogramBuffer;
404	
405	    if (buf) {
406	        DrvISCObj.awb.count[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] = 0;
407	        for (i = 0; i < ISC_HIST_ENTRIES; i++) {
408	            if (*buf) {
409	                if (!hist_min)
410	                    hist_min = i;
411	                DrvISCObj.awb.white_count[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] = 0;
412	                hist_max = i;
413	            }
414	            DrvISCObj.awb.count[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] += (*buf) * i;
415	            DrvISCObj.awb.white_count[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] += (*buf++) * i;
416	        }
417	        if (!hist_min)
418	            hist_min = 1;
419	
420	        DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] = hist_min;
421	        DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] = hist_max;
422	    }
423	}
424	
425	static void DRV_ISC_AWB_Update(void) {
426	    int32_t wb_offset[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};
427	    uint32_t gain[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};
428	    uint32_t a_max = 0;
429	    uint64_t hist_avg = 0;
430	    uint32_t k[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};
431	    uint32_t x[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};
432	
433	    a_max = DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[0];
434	    for (uint8_t b = 1; b < ISC_BAYER_COUNT; b++) {
435	        if (DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[b] > a_max)
436	            a_max = DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[b];
437	    }
438	    hist_avg = (uint64_t) DrvISCObj.awb.count[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GR] + (uint64_t) DrvISCObj.awb.count[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GB];
439	    hist_avg >>= 1;
440	    for (uint8_t b = 0; b < ISC_BAYER_COUNT; b++) {
441	        if (DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[b] != 0) {
442	            /* Convert 12 bits pipline to 9 bits. */
443	            wb_offset[b] = -((DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[b] - 1) << 3);
444	        }
445	        k[b] = (hist_avg << 9) / DrvISCObj.awb.count[b];
446	
447	        /* the a_max is the maximum value of Rhigh,Ghigh,Bhigh. We set the maximum values of the original image to be the thresholds, avoiding the over stretching. */
448	        x[b] = (a_max << 9) / (DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[b] - DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[b] + 1);
```

        DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] = hist_min;
        DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode] = hist_max;

static void DRV_ISC_AWB_Update(void) {
    int32_t wb_offset[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};
    uint32_t gain[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};
    uint32_t a_max = 0;
    uint64_t hist_avg = 0;
    uint32_t k[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};
    uint32_t x[ISC_BAYER_COUNT] = {0};

    a_max = DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[0];
    for (uint8_t b = 1; b < ISC_BAYER_COUNT; b++) {
        if (DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[b] > a_max)
            a_max = DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[b];
    }
    hist_avg = (uint64_t) DrvISCObj.awb.count[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GR] + (uint64_t) DrvISCObj.awb.count[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GB];
    hist_avg >>= 1;
    for (uint8_t b = 0; b < ISC_BAYER_COUNT; b++) {
        if (DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[b] != 0) {
            /* Convert 12 bits pipline to 9 bits. */
            wb_offset[b] = -((DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[b] - 1) << 3);
        }
        k[b] = (hist_avg << 9) / DrvISCObj.awb.count[b];

        /* the a_max is the maximum value of Rhigh,Ghigh,Bhigh. We set the maximum values of the original image to be the thresholds, avoiding the over stretching. */
        x[b] = (a_max << 9) / (DrvISCObj.awb.hist_max[b] - DrvISCObj.awb.hist_min[b] + 1);
        x[b] = (x[b] > (3 << 9)) ? (3 << 9) : x[b];
        gain[b] = x[b] * k[b];
        gain[b] >>= 9;
    }

    ISC_WB_Set_Bayer_Color(wb_offset[ISC_HISTOGRAM_R],
            wb_offset[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GR],
            wb_offset[ISC_HISTOGRAM_B],
            wb_offset[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GB],
            gain[ISC_HISTOGRAM_R],
            gain[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GR],
            gain[ISC_HISTOGRAM_B],
            gain[ISC_HISTOGRAM_GB]);

    ISC_Update_Profile();
}

static void DRV_ISC_XDMA_Read_Histogram(void) {

    if (DrvISCObj.histogramBuffer)
        XDMAC_ChannelTransfer(DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.channel,
            (void *) &ISC_REGS->ISC_HIS_ENTRY[0], (void *)
            DrvISCObj.histogramBuffer, ISC_HIST_ENTRIES * 4);
}

void DRV_ISC_AWB_Algo(void) {
    switch (DrvISCObj.awb.state) {
        case AWB_INIT:
            ISC_Histogram_Configure(DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode, ISC_WB_Get_Bayer_Pattern(), 0);
            ISC_Update_Profile();
            if (DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode != (ISC_REGS->ISC_HIS_CFG & ISC_HIS_CFG_MODE_Msk))
                break;

            ISC_Clear_Histogram_Table();
            DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.dma_histo_done = false;
            ISC_Update_Histogram_Table();
            DrvISCObj.awb.state = AWB_WAIT_HIS_READY;
            break;
        case AWB_WAIT_HIS_READY:
            if (!DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.dma_histo_ready)
                break;
            DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.dma_histo_ready = false;
            DRV_ISC_XDMA_Read_Histogram();
            DrvISCObj.awb.state = AWB_WAIT_DMA_READY;
            break;
        case AWB_WAIT_DMA_READY:
            if (!DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.dma_histo_done)
                break;
            DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.dma_histo_done = false;
            DRV_ISC_AWB_CountUp();
            DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode++;
            if (DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode < ISC_BAYER_COUNT) {
                DrvISCObj.awb.state = AWB_INIT;
            } else {
                DrvISCObj.awb.state = AWB_WAIT_ISC_PERFORMED;
            }
            break;
        case AWB_WAIT_ISC_PERFORMED:
            DRV_ISC_AWB_Update();
            DrvISCObj.awb.op_mode = 0;
            DrvISCObj.awb.state = AWB_INIT;
            break;
    }
}

DRV_ISC_OBJ* DRV_ISC_Initialize(void) {
    ISC_Initialize();

    return &DrvISCObj;
}

53	    uint32_t sr;
54	    int counter = 1000;
55	
56	    while (ISC_Sync_InProgress());
57	    ISC_REGS->ISC_CTRLEN = ISC_CTRLEN_UPPRO_Msk;
58	    sr = ISC_REGS->ISC_CTRLSR;
59	    while ((sr & ISC_CTRLEN_UPPRO_Msk) && counter--) {
60	        DelayUS(2000);
61	        sr = ISC_REGS->ISC_CTRLSR;
62	    }
63	    if (counter < 0) {

## CSI-2 RX Pipeline Initialization Map (600-word report)

Based on analysis of marvin (target) and emirror (reference) projects, here's the territory map for bringing up the SAM9X75 CSI-2 receive pipeline from bare Harmony firmware.

### 1. CSI (D-PHY RX) Initialization

**Function signatures** — marvin `/Users/gregmrozek/Projects/microchip/guitar-pic/firmware/marvin/default/src/config/default/vision/drivers/csi/drv_csi.h:28,162`:
- `DRV_CSI_OBJ* DRV_CSI_Initalize(void)` — allocates and returns static `csiObj`, returns NULL on failure
- `bool DRV_CSI_Configure(DRV_CSI_OBJ* devObj)` — configures PHY with object state

**Data structure** — drv_csi.h:15-24:
```c
typedef struct {
    uint8_t numLanes;           // CSI_NUM_LANES from config
    uint8_t csiDataType;        // CSI2_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888 (0x24)
    uint8_t csiDataId;          // Virtual channel: 0
    uint8_t csiVirtualChannel;  // Virtual channel: 0
    uint8_t csiBitRate;         // Hardcoded 0x16 in init
    uint32_t csiFps;            // Default 150, sensor-dependent
    uint32_t csiFrameWidth;     // 640 default, updated by camera driver
    uint32_t csiFrameHeight;    // 480 default, updated by camera driver
} DRV_CSI_OBJ;
```

**Init sequence** — drv_csi.c:162-174:
```c
DRV_CSI_OBJ* DRV_CSI_Initalize(void) {
    csiObj.numLanes = CSI_NUM_LANES;         // = CSI_DATA_LANES_2 (marvin config)
    csiObj.csiDataType = CSI_DATA_FORMAT_TYPE; // = CSI2_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888
    csiObj.csiBitRate = 0x16;
    csiObj.csiFrameWidth = 640;
    csiObj.csiFrameHeight = 480;
    csiObj.csiFps = 150;
    csiObj.csiDataId = 0;
    csiObj.csiVirtualChannel = 0;
    return &csiObj;
}
```

**Configuration** — drv_csi.c:133-160: Calls plib functions CSI_Reset(), CSI_Shutdown(), CSI_Reset_DPhy(), CSI_Analog_Init(bitrate, lanes), CSI_Exit_Shutdown(), CSI_Exit_Reset_DPhy(), CSI_Configure_Lane(lanes), CSI_Configure_DataId(), CSI_Exit_Reset().

**Critical params**: numLanes (2 for your case), bitrate 0x16, dataType 0x24 (RGB888), width/height updated from sensor after CAMERA_Open().

### 2. CSI2DC Initialization

**Function signatures** — drv_csi2dc.h:46-48:
- `DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ* DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize(void)` — returns static object
- `bool DRV_CSI2DC_Configure(DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ* devObj)` — configures data pipes

**Data structure** — drv_csi2dc.h:28-44:
```c
typedef struct {
    uint8_t videoPipeChannelId;    // CSI2DC_VIDEO_PIPE_CHANNEL_ID
    uint8_t dataPipeChannelId;     // CSI2DC_DATA_PIPE_CHANNEL_ID
    uint8_t videoPipeDataType;     // CSI2DC_VIDEO_PIPE_FORMAT_TYPE
    uint8_t dataPipeDataType;      // CSI2DC_DATA_PIPE_FORMAT_TYPE
    CSI2DC_BUS_MODE busMode;       // CSI2DC_BUS_CSI2_DPHY
    CSI2DC_DMA csi2dcDma;          // DMA chunk size, count, enable flag
    bool enableMIPIFreeRun;
    bool videoPipeAlign;
    bool enableDataPipe;
} DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ;
```

**Init sequence** — emirror camera.c:515-527: After DRV_ISC_Initialize(), call DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize(), then override videoPipeDataType/dataPipeDataType from CAMERA_INIT if needed (CSI2DC_DATA_FORMAT_RAW8 default).

**DMA config** — drv_csi2dc.h:28-32: CSI2DC_DMA.enableDMA flag, chunk sizes 1/2/4/8/16 beats, count field.

### 3. ISC Initialization + DMA + Callback

**Function signatures** — drv_isc.h:176-188:
- `DRV_ISC_OBJ* DRV_ISC_Initialize(void)` — calls plib ISC_Initialize(), returns static DrvISCObj
- `uint8_t DRV_ISC_Configure(DRV_ISC_OBJ* iscObj)` — configures PFE, DPC, WB, gamma, RLP, DMA; disables ISC interrupt at start (line 228), enables at end (390-392)
- `uint8_t DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA(DRV_ISC_OBJ* iscObj)` — builds DMA descriptor chain in isc_dma_pool
- `bool DRV_ISC_Start_Capture(DRV_ISC_OBJ* iscObj)` — waits for ISC_INTSR_VD, retries up to 1000 iterations

**DMA pool** — drv_isc.c:20-26: Static union isc_dma_pool with 3 views (packed, semiplanar, planar), each with up to ISC_MAX_DMA_DESC (10) descriptors:
```c
__attribute__((__section__(".region_cache_aligned"))) __attribute__((__aligned__(32))) ISC_DEVICE_DMA_Pool isc_dma_pool;
```

**Descriptor structure** — drv_isc.h:96-121: DRV_ISC_DMA_VIEW0 (packed), VIEW1 (semiplanar), VIEW2 (planar). Each has ctrl, nextDesc, address(es), stride(es).

**Frame-complete callback** — drv_isc.c:45-55: ISC_Handler() checks ISC_INTSR_DDONE_Msk. On match, bumps frameIndex (wraps at dmaDescSize), calls `iscObj->dma.callback((uintptr_t)&iscObj)`.

**Callback registration** — emirror camera.c:227-229: Set in CAMERA_configure() after CAMERA_Open():
```c
pDrvObject->iscObj->dma.address0 = (uint32_t) GBuffer;
pDrvObject->iscObj->dma.size = pDrvObject->bufferSize;
pDrvObject->iscObj->dma.callback = CAMERA_ISC_Callback;  // user callback wrapper
```

**Interrupt enable** — drv_isc.c:390-392: ISC_Enable_Interrupt(ISC_INTEN_VD(1) | ISC_INTEN_DDONE(1)) after DMA config. ISC_Interrupt_Status() clears on read.

### 4. Framebuffer

**Allocation** — emirror camera.c:50-51:
```c
__attribute__((__section__(".region_cache"))) __attribute__((__aligned__(32))) 
    static uint8_t GBuffer[1920 * 1080 * 4 * DMA_MAX_BUFFERS];
```

**Linker section** — emirror ddram.ld:140-145: `.region_cache_aligned (NOLOAD)` placed in main >ram (not nocache). Aligned 32-byte boundary for DMA cache coherence.

**Size calculation** — camera.h:31: `FRAME_BUFFER_SIZE(W, H, BPP) = W * H * (BPP/8)`. Per-frame size multiplied by DMA_MAX_BUFFERS (2).

**DMA_MAX_BUFFERS** — camera.h:28: Defines 2 frame buffers for double-buffering. frameIndex wraps 0..1.

### 5. Order of Operations (emirror)

camera.c:428-627 (CAMERA_Initialize):
1. `DRV_ISC_Initialize()` → plib ISC_Initialize() [clocks only]
2. If SAM9X7: `DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize()`, store object
3. If ISC_ENABLE_MIPI: `DRV_CSI_Initalize()`, store object
4. Set ISC config fields from CAMERA_INIT (inputFormat, inputBits, layout, enable flags)
5. CAMERA_Task() invoked state machine → CAMERA_OPEN state
6. CAMERA_Open() (camera.c:340-401):
   - DRV_ImageSensor_Configure() + GetConfig() → get width, height, bitwidth
   - Update CSI object width/height (line 389-390)
   - DRV_CSI2DC_Configure() (line 383)
   - DRV_CSI_Configure() (line 392)
   - CAMERA_configure() → set DMA addresses, callback, call DRV_ISC_Configure()
7. CAMERA_Start_Capture() → DRV_ImageSensor_Start(), DRV_ISC_Start_Capture(), SYS_INT_SourceEnable(ID_ISC)

### 6. Gotchas & Constraints

- **ISC sync domain**: ISC_Sync_InProgress() check (plib_isc.c:22-24) required before writing ISC_CTRLEN/CTRLDIS
- **Interrupt IDs**: SYS_INT_SourceDisable/Enable(ID_CSI2DC), SYS_INT_SourceDisable/Enable(ID_ISC) — device.h defines
- **Cache coherence**: DMA pool + framebuffer both `.region_cache_aligned(32)`, not `.region_nocache`. Requires SYS_CACHE_CleanDCache_by_Addr() on descriptor pool (drv_isc.c:110, 139, 166)
- **ISC clock**: plib ISC_Initialize() (plib_isc.c:823) enables master clock (MCK_DIV, MCK_SEL) and ISP clock, waits ISC_CLKSR ready
- **Start capture retry**: DRV_ISC_Start_Capture() polls ISC_INTSR_VD for up to 1000ms; must call a second time after detecting VD (drv_isc.c:74-80)
- **Profile update latency**: ISC_Update_Profile() waits up to 2ms per loop iteration; called after DMA config and inside AWB algo (plib_isc.c:52-67)
- **Sensor dependency**: CSI bitrate 0x16 hardcoded but real value depends on lanes, fps, bpp. Sensor config must be loaded before calling CSI_Configure()

**For your RGB888 720x480 case with frame-complete interrupt counting**: Allocate 720*480*4*2 bytes (5.76 MB) in `.region_cache_aligned`, set numLanes=2, dataType=RGB888(0x24), DMA layout=ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED32, register callback to increment counter on ISC_INTSR_DDONE, call DRV_CSI_Initalize() → DRV_CSI_Configure() → DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize() → DRV_CSI2DC_Configure() → DRV_ISC_Initialize() → DRV_ISC_Configure() + DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA() → DRV_ISC_Start_Capture() → SYS_INT_SourceEnable(ID_ISC).

Comprehensive survey back. Let me lay out Phase 5 before implementing — it's bigger than previous phases and there's one structural fork to decide.

**Phase 5 scope (in brief):**

Initialize three drivers (CSI D-PHY RX → CSI2DC → ISC), allocate a framebuffer in DDR3 with cache alignment, configure ISC DMA to write into it, register a frame-complete callback, start capture, and print a frame counter from the watcher so we can see "are we receiving ~60 frames/sec".

**Key facts from the survey:**

- API shape: `DRV_CSI_Initalize()` / `DRV_CSI_Configure()` (note the typo "Initalize" — that's literal, from MCC), same pattern for CSI2DC and ISC. Each returns a pointer to a static object we fill in with width/height/format/etc.
- Frame-complete callback registered as `iscObj->dma.callback` — ISC handler calls it on `DDONE`.
- Framebuffer sits in a `.region_cache_aligned` linker section (32-byte aligned for DMA cache coherence). emirror uses `__attribute__((__section__(".region_cache")))`.
- For 720×480 ARGB32 × 2 buffers = ~2.7 MB in DDR3. Trivial for our 256 MB.
- `DRV_ISC_Start_Capture()` polls `ISC_INTSR_VD` for up to ~1 s — could briefly block our watcher on startup. Tolerable for bring-up.

**Structural question:** everything we've written so far lives in `tc358743.c` (~900 lines). Phase 5 adds ~150 more lines of unrelated concern (SAM9X75 ISC side, not TC358743). Two options:

162	static void dw_dphy_write_msk(struct dw_dphy_rx *dev, u32 address, u32 data, u8 shift,
163			       u8 width)
164	{
165		u32 temp = dw_dphy_read(dev, address);
166		u32 mask = (1 << width) - 1;
167	
168		temp &= ~(mask << shift);
169		temp |= (data & mask) << shift;
170		dw_dphy_write(dev, address, temp);
171	}

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:17:05Z)**_

Now I can see the real picture. From the Linux DWC D-PHY header:

```
HS_RX_CTRL_LANE0 = 0x42
HSFREQRANGE_8BIT = 0x44           ← chip-wide bit-rate range register
HS_RX_CTRL_LANE1 = 0x52
HS_RX_CTRL_LANE2 = 0x82           ← note jump from 0x52
HS_RX_CTRL_LANE3 = 0x92
```

So in canonical DWC, `0x44` is **HSFREQRANGE** (a single chip-wide bit-rate register), not Lane 0's HS RX control. The HS_RX_CTRL-for-lane registers are at `0x42/0x52/0x82/0x92`.

The plib_csi.c addresses (`0x34`/`0x44`/`0x54`/`0x64`/`0x74`) don't match that exactly. Could be a different DWC PHY variant, could be Microchip's own variant. Since you're the one who knows it has been partially-working with these addresses, I'll trust that the addresses-as-written (0x34/0x44/0x54/...) are correct for this hardware.

**Here's my read of the bugs, from most to least certain:**

1. **Lane 1 missing bit_rate** (your primary concern). After line 145, same 3 lines as 134-136 should appear for Lane 1.
2. **Lane 2 address typo**: lines 148 and 156 have `TESTDIN(0x24)` but the comment right above says `code = 0x64`. The 0x24 looks like a copy-paste error — should be 0x64.
3. **3-lane case skips Lane 1 entirely**: the `else if (nlanes == CSI_DATA_LANES_3)` never runs Lane 1 code, because the Lane 1 block only runs in the `nlanes == CSI_DATA_LANES_2` branch. For a 3-lane config, Lane 1 would be un-initialized.
4. **4-lane case skips Lane 1** for the same reason.
5. **Missing bit_rate for clock lane, Lane 2, Lane 3** — same pattern as #1 for everyone except Lane 0.

**My recommendation is a refactor:** extract a per-lane helper, use it for Lane 0 + each additional lane gated by `nlanes >=`. Much cleaner than the if/else-if chain, and fixes all five issues in one shot.

Clear answer from Linux driver. Looking at [dw-dphy-rx.c:345-350](../linux-at91/drivers/media/platform/dwc/dw-dphy-rx.c#L345-L350):

```c
if (input_freq < 2000)
    dw_dphy_te_write(dphy, HS_RX_CTRL_LANE0, 0xC0);

if (input_freq < 1000) {
    dw_dphy_te_write(dphy, HS_RX_CTRL_LANE1, 0xC0);
    dw_dphy_te_write(dphy, HS_RX_CTRL_LANE2, 0xC0);
    dw_dphy_te_write(dphy, HS_RX_CTRL_LANE3, 0xC0);
}
```

**No, the clock lane does NOT get a per-lane HS RX control write in Linux.** Linux programs:

- `HS_RX_CTRL_LANEn` — for data lanes only (0-3).
- `HSFREQRANGE_8BIT` — once, chip-wide, separate register (not per-lane).
- `OSC_FREQ_TARGET_RXn` — per data lane, not clock lane.

The clock lane is auto-handled by the global settings in Linux. So extending the plib_csi.c pattern to the clock lane would be adding untested-against-reference behavior.

**Updated recommendation:** refactor data lanes only, keep clock lane's init (lines 118-125) untouched. Here's the plan:

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:23:14Z)**_

Agreed — leave MCC alone here, set from our side. Rationale:

**Why changing MCC is less good:**

1. MCC regen will clobber it (same risk as plib_csi.c fix).
2. `csiObj` fields are already a "caller fills these in" interface — the `0x16` in MCC is effectively a default, not a configuration we need to make authoritative.
3. We already need to override `csiFrameWidth`/`csiFrameHeight` anyway (MCC's 640×480 defaults don't match our 720×480), so our isc_capture code is already going to be populating the CSI object. Adding `csiBitRate = 0x14` alongside is one more line in our code, zero additional MCC-fragility.

**Pattern for our isc_capture:**

```c
csiObj = DRV_CSI_Initalize();
csiObj->csiBitRate     = 0x14;
csiObj->csiFrameWidth  = 720;
csiObj->csiFrameHeight = 480;
csiObj->csiFps         = 60;
// csiDataType, numLanes, csiDataId, csiVirtualChannel kept at MCC defaults
```

This keeps the `plib_csi.c` fix as our ONE MCC-modification (the bug fix), and everything else stays in our isc_capture.c where it belongs.

On your broader question about "worth cleaning up csiBitRate to be more flexible" — not worth it. The MCC-style "set default then caller overrides" is fine; we just don't rely on the defaults.

Let me note this in the journal and then we can move on to writing isc_capture.c.

static DRV_ISC_OBJ DrvISCObj;

static void DelayUS(uint32_t us) {
    SYS_TIME_HANDLE timer = SYS_TIME_HANDLE_INVALID;
    if (SYS_TIME_DelayUS(us, &timer) != SYS_TIME_SUCCESS)
        return;
    while (SYS_TIME_DelayIsComplete(timer) == false);
}

void ISC_Handler(void) {
    volatile const uint32_t status = ISC_Interrupt_Status();
    if ((status & ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk) == ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk) {
        ISC_Disable_Interrupt(ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk);
        DrvISCObj.awb.hist_dma.dma_histo_ready = true;
        ISC_Enable_Interrupt(ISC_INTSR_HISDONE_Msk);
    }

    if ((status & ISC_INTSR_DDONE_Msk) == ISC_INTSR_DDONE_Msk) {
        ISC_Disable_Interrupt(ISC_INTEN_DDONE_Msk);
        if (DrvISCObj.frameIndex == (DrvISCObj.dmaDescSize - 1))
            DrvISCObj.frameIndex = 0;
        else
            DrvISCObj.frameIndex++;

        if (DrvISCObj.dma.callback)
            DrvISCObj.dma.callback((uintptr_t) & DrvISCObj);
        ISC_Enable_Interrupt(ISC_INTEN_DDONE_Msk);
    }
    if ((status & ISC_INTSR_VD_Msk) == ISC_INTSR_VD_Msk) {
        DrvISCObj.frameCount++;
    }
```

#include "isc_capture.h"

#include <stdbool.h>
#include <stddef.h>
#include <stdint.h>
#include <stdio.h>

#include "definitions.h"

#define ISC_CAP_MAX_W        1920u
#define ISC_CAP_MAX_H        1080u
#define ISC_CAP_BPP          4u    /* ARGB32 */
#define ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS  2u
#define ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE  0x14u

static __attribute__((__section__(".region_cache_aligned")))
       __attribute__((__aligned__(32)))
       uint8_t g_framebuffer[ISC_CAP_MAX_W * ISC_CAP_MAX_H * ISC_CAP_BPP * ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS];

static DRV_CSI_OBJ*    csiObj;
static DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ* csi2dcObj;
static DRV_ISC_OBJ*    iscObj;

static volatile uint32_t g_frame_count;
static bool              g_running;

static void isc_frame_done(uintptr_t ctx)
{
    (void)ctx;
    g_frame_count++;
}

void ISC_Capture_Initialize(void)
{
    iscObj    = DRV_ISC_Initialize();
    csi2dcObj = DRV_CSI2DC_Initalize();
    csiObj    = DRV_CSI_Initalize();

    if (iscObj == NULL || csi2dcObj == NULL || csiObj == NULL)
    {
        printf("ISC_Capture: driver init returned NULL\r\n");
        return;
    }

    iscObj->inputFormat           = ISC_INPUT_FORMAT_TYPE;
    iscObj->inputBits             = ISC_INPUT_BIT_WIDTH;
    iscObj->rlpMode               = ISC_OUTPUT_FORMAT_TYPE;
    iscObj->layout                = ISC_OUTPUT_LAYOUT_TYPE;
    iscObj->bayerPattern          = ISC_BAYER_PATTERN_TYPE;
    iscObj->enableMIPI            = ISC_ENABLE_MIPI_INTERFACE;
    iscObj->enableVideoMode       = ISC_ENABLE_VIDEO_MODE;
    iscObj->enableProgressiveMode = ISC_ENABLE_PROGRESSIVE_MODE;
    iscObj->enableScaling         = ISC_ENABLE_SCALING;
    iscObj->dpc.enableDPC         = ISC_ENABLE_DPC;
    iscObj->dpc.enableGDC         = ISC_ENABLE_GDC;
    iscObj->dpc.enableBLC         = ISC_ENABLE_BLC;
    iscObj->cbc.enableCBC         = ISC_ENABLE_BRIGHTNESS_CONTRAST;
    iscObj->whiteBalance.enableWB = ISC_ENABLE_WHITE_BALANCE;
    iscObj->gamma.enableGamma     = ISC_ENABLE_GAMMA;
    iscObj->enableHistogram       = ISC_ENABLE_HISTOGRAM;
    iscObj->dmaDescSize           = (uint8_t)ISC_CAP_NUM_BUFFERS;
    iscObj->dma.callback          = isc_frame_done;

    /* DRV_CSI_Initalize hardcodes csiBitRate = 0x16; override here. */
    csiObj->csiBitRate = ISC_CAP_CSI_BITRATE;

    printf("ISC_Capture: initialized\r\n");
}

bool ISC_Capture_Start(uint32_t width, uint32_t height)
{
    if (g_running) { ISC_Capture_Stop(); }

    if (width == 0u || height == 0u
        || width > ISC_CAP_MAX_W || height > ISC_CAP_MAX_H)
    {
        printf("ISC_Capture: %lux%lu out of range\r\n",
               (unsigned long)width, (unsigned long)height);
        return false;
    }

    uint32_t frame_size = width * height * ISC_CAP_BPP;

    csiObj->csiFrameWidth  = width;
    csiObj->csiFrameHeight = height;
    csiObj->csiFps         = 60u;

    iscObj->imageWidth   = (uint16_t)width;
    iscObj->imageHeight  = (uint16_t)height;
    iscObj->outputWidth  = (uint16_t)width;
    iscObj->outputHeight = (uint16_t)height;
    iscObj->dma.address0 = (uint32_t)(uintptr_t)g_framebuffer;
    iscObj->dma.size     = frame_size;

    g_frame_count = 0u;

    if (!DRV_CSI_Configure(csiObj))
    {
        printf("ISC_Capture: DRV_CSI_Configure failed\r\n");
        return false;
    }
    if (!DRV_CSI2DC_Configure(csi2dcObj))
    {
        printf("ISC_Capture: DRV_CSI2DC_Configure failed\r\n");
        return false;
    }
    if (DRV_ISC_Configure(iscObj) != 0u)
    {
        printf("ISC_Capture: DRV_ISC_Configure failed\r\n");
        return false;
    }
    if (DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA(iscObj) != 0u)
    {
        printf("ISC_Capture: DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA failed\r\n");
        return false;
    }
    if (!DRV_ISC_Start_Capture(iscObj))
    {
        printf("ISC_Capture: DRV_ISC_Start_Capture failed\r\n");
        return false;
    }

    SYS_INT_SourceEnable(ID_ISC);
    g_running = true;
    printf("ISC_Capture: started %lux%lu ARGB32 (%lu bytes/frame)\r\n",
           (unsigned long)width, (unsigned long)height,
           (unsigned long)frame_size);
    return true;
}

void ISC_Capture_Stop(void)
{
    if (!g_running) { return; }
    SYS_INT_SourceDisable(ID_ISC);
    DRV_ISC_Stop_Capture();
    g_running = false;
    printf("ISC_Capture: stopped\r\n");
}

uint32_t ISC_Capture_FrameCount(void)
{
    return g_frame_count;
}

bool ISC_Capture_IsRunning(void)
{
    return g_running;
}

```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:33:52Z)**_

You're right to push back. Let me sketch the dependency options honestly:

**Current plan (what I was writing):** `tc358743.c` → `isc_capture.c`. The TC358743 chip driver reaches downward into the SAM9X75 SoC RX driver. That IS upside-down — a bridge-chip driver shouldn't know anything about the SoC's capture pipeline.

**Proper layering options:**

**Option A — app.c coordinates.** Both modules become pure drivers:
- `tc358743.c` exposes state: `TC358743_IsLocked()`, `TC358743_GetDetectedFormat(&w, &h)`. No mention of ISC.
- `isc_capture.c` unchanged (already pure).
- `app.c` polls `TC358743_IsLocked()` each `APP_Tasks` tick, tracks last state, calls `ISC_Capture_Start(w, h)` on 0→1 and `ISC_Capture_Stop()` on 1→0.

  Clean layering. `app.c` grows a small state machine.

**Option B — split out a coordinator.** The "watcher" logic (polling SYS_STATUS, calling `enable_stream`, starting ISC) really isn't TC358743-specific — it's orchestration. Move it into a new `hdmi_capture.c` (or similar) that:
- Owns the polling / state-machine.
- Calls into `tc358743.c` for bridge-chip actions (IsLocked, enable_stream, GetDetectedFormat).
- Calls into `isc_capture.c` for SoC-side actions.
- tc358743.c shrinks to just the chip driver (init, register helpers, `enable_stream`, `IsLocked`, `GetDetectedFormat`).

  Most architecturally pure. Three files in the capture stack: `tc358743` (bridge) + `isc_capture` (SoC) + `hdmi_capture` (orchestrator).

**Option C — keep the coupling, own it.** Acknowledge that our `tc358743.c` is already not a pure bridge-chip driver (it has a watcher, printf output, logic about when to stream-enable). So this is really `hdmi_source.c` misnamed. Accept the `#include "isc_capture.h"` and call it done.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:34:35Z)**_

<tool-use data-tool-type="generic" data-tool-name="AskUserQuestion"><details>
<summary>Tool use: **AskUserQuestion**</summary>
**How to structure the tc358743 / isc_capture relationship?**

Options:
- **Option A — app.c coordinates (Recommended)** - tc358743.c exposes state-query API (IsLocked, GetDetectedFormat); isc_capture.c unchanged; app.c polls and drives transitions. Clean horizontal layering, small change scope.
- **Option B — separate coordinator file** - New hdmi_capture.c holds the watcher/state-machine, calls tc358743.c (pure bridge driver) and isc_capture.c (pure SoC driver). Most architecturally pure but most refactoring — large chunks of tc358743.c's watcher move out.
- **Option C — accept the coupling** - tc358743.c #includes isc_capture.h and calls Start/Stop directly. Simplest, but acknowledges tc358743.c is really 'hdmi_source.c' in disguise.


**Answer:** Option A — app.c coordinates (Recommended)
</details></tool-use>

873	    if (height != NULL) { *height = h; }
874	    return true;
875	}
876	
877	static void log_status_change(uint8_t prev, uint8_t cur)
878	{
879	    printf("TC358743: SYS_STATUS 0x%02X->0x%02X [%s%s%s%s%s%s]\r\n",
880	           prev, cur,
881	           (cur & MASK_S_DDC5V)    ? "DDC5V "  : "",
882	           (cur & MASK_S_TMDS)     ? "TMDS "   : "",
883	           (cur & MASK_S_PHY_PLL)  ? "PLL "    : "",
884	           (cur & MASK_S_PHY_SCDT) ? "SCDT "   : "",
885	           (cur & MASK_S_HDMI)     ? "HDMI "   : "",
886	           (cur & MASK_S_SYNC)     ? "SYNC"    : "");
887	
888	    bool sync_now      = (cur  & MASK_S_SYNC) != 0u;
889	    bool sync_previous = (prev & MASK_S_SYNC) != 0u;
890	    if (sync_now && !sync_previous)
891	    {
892	        (void)read_detected_format(NULL, NULL);
893	        if (tc358743_enable_stream(true))
894	        {
895	            printf("TC358743: CSI stream enabled\r\n");
896	            log_csi_status();
897	        }
898	        else
899	        {
900	            printf("TC358743: CSI stream enable failed\r\n");
901	        }
902	    }
903	    else if (!sync_now && sync_previous)
904	    {
905	        if (tc358743_enable_stream(false))
906	        {
907	            printf("TC358743: CSI stream disabled\r\n");
908	        }
909	    }
910	}
911	
912	void TC358743_Tasks(void)
913	{
914	    static SYS_TIME_HANDLE pollHandle = SYS_TIME_HANDLE_INVALID;
915	    static uint8_t         lastStatus = 0u;
916	    static bool            firstPoll  = true;
917	
918	    if (i2cHandle == DRV_HANDLE_INVALID) { return; }
919	
920	    if (pollHandle != SYS_TIME_HANDLE_INVALID
921	        && !SYS_TIME_DelayIsComplete(pollHandle))
922	    {
923	        return;
924	    }
925	
926	    uint8_t sys_status;
927	    if (tc358743_rd8(SYS_STATUS, &sys_status))
928	    {
929	        if (firstPoll)
930	        {
931	            firstPoll = false;
932	            lastStatus = sys_status;
933	            printf("TC358743: watcher start; SYS_STATUS=0x%02X\r\n", sys_status);
934	            if (sys_status & MASK_S_SYNC)
935	            {
936	                (void)read_detected_format(NULL, NULL);
937	                if (tc358743_enable_stream(true))
938	                {
939	                    printf("TC358743: CSI stream enabled\r\n");
940	                    log_csi_status();
941	                }
942	            }
943	        }
944	        else if (sys_status != lastStatus)
945	        {
946	            log_status_change(lastStatus, sys_status);
947	            lastStatus = sys_status;
948	        }
949	    }
950	
951	    pollHandle = SYS_TIME_HANDLE_INVALID;
952	    (void)SYS_TIME_DelayMS(STATUS_POLL_MS, &pollHandle);
953	}
954

Phase 5 implementation is in. Summary:

**Files:**

- **New: [isc_capture.h](firmware/marvin/default/src/isc_capture.h)** — public API: `Initialize`, `Start(w,h)`, `Stop`, `FrameCount`, `IsRunning`.
- **New: [isc_capture.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/isc_capture.c)** — pure SoC-side capture driver. ~140 lines. Initializes ISC/CSI2DC/CSI, overrides `csiBitRate = 0x14`, allocates framebuffer (`.region_cache_aligned`, 32-byte aligned, sized for max 1920x1080 ARGB32 × 2), DMA callback increments counter.
- **Modified: [tc358743.c/h](firmware/marvin/default/src/tc358743.c)** — reverted the `#include "isc_capture.h"`; added state-query API (`TC358743_IsLocked`, `TC358743_GetDetectedFormat`) backed by module-scope caches updated by the watcher.
- **Modified: [app.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/app.c)** — `APP_Initialize` calls both `ISC_Capture_Initialize` and `TC358743_Initialize`. `APP_Tasks` calls `TC358743_Tasks`, then two new orchestrator helpers: `app_coordinate_capture()` (maps TC358743 lock transitions → ISC Start/Stop) and `app_report_fps()` (prints `ISC: N fps` once per second when capture is running).
- **Modified: [user.cmake](firmware/marvin/cmake/marvin/default/user.cmake)** — added `isc_capture.c` to the build.

**Architecture:** Both drivers are pure (no horizontal coupling). `app.c` orchestrates.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:44:55Z)**_

Two issues, one quick code fix and one diagnostic question:

**Fix first: don't retry every second.** `app_coordinate_capture` currently retries whenever `capture_started == false`, which means each failed `DRV_ISC_Start_Capture` (which itself blocks for ~1 s polling VD) gets re-attempted. Let me mark "capture attempted" once we've called Start, regardless of success — a true retry should wait for source unlock/relock.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:45:26Z)**_

Now for the real issue: `DRV_ISC_Start_Capture` polls `ISC_INTSR_VD` for 1 second waiting for vsync from ISC. Not seeing VD means ISC never got a frame-start — so either D-PHY isn't decoding, CSI2DC isn't forwarding, or ISC's sync detection is off. TC358743 is transmitting (TXACT=1) so the data is definitely on the wire.

This is where your "other patches" probably come in — the CSI RX path almost certainly needs fixes.

Diagnostic added. After flashing, the log will show two register dumps — one just before `DRV_ISC_Start_Capture` (pre-start) and one after it fails (post-fail).

**What the dumps will tell us:**

- **`CSI2DC_FNVC0R`** — frames received on Virtual Channel 0. If this is nonzero on post-fail, data IS reaching CSI2DC (problem is ISC-side). If zero, CSI RX never locked.
- **`CSI_PHY_RX` bits 0-3** — which data lanes are in HS-Receive. Should have bit 0 and bit 1 set for our 2-lane config when signal is present.
- **`CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE`** — which lanes are in LP11. Inverse of HS; both should toggle as frames arrive.
- **`CSI_INT_ST_MAIN`** — which error categories fired.
- **`CSI_INT_ST_PHY_FATAL`** — bit 0 default is 1; non-bit-0 bits = D-PHY lane errors.
- **`CSI_INT_ST_PKT_FATAL`** — bad SoT, bad ECC, etc. Nonzero = broken packets on the wire.
- **`CSI_INT_ST_FRAME_FATAL`** — frame-level errors.
- **`CSI2DC_GSR`** — overall CSI2DC state.
- **`ISC_INTSR`** — what ISC saw (if bit for VD is in here without `_VD(1)` match, could be edge case).

Flash and paste the output. That'll localize the break between "PHY not locking", "packets arriving but malformed", or "CSI2DC/ISC handoff broken."

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:51:46Z)**_

Now we have a clear picture. Key findings:

**`CSI_PHY_RX = 0x00010000`** — this is literally the **reset value** of that register (`CSI_PHY_RX_RESETVALUE = 0x10000` per the pack header). Bits 0-3 (data lane HS-receive) are **all 0**. The D-PHY RX hasn't transitioned any lane to high-speed mode.

**`CSI_PHY_STOPSTATE = 0x00000003`** — data lanes 0 and 1 are stuck in LP11 (stop state). The PHY is seeing LP idle on the lanes, not HS bursts.

**`CSI2DC_FNVC0R = 0`** — zero frames reached CSI2DC. Confirms data isn't making it past the PHY.

**`CSI_INT_ST_* all 0`** — no errors detected. Not even PHY fatal. So the PHY didn't detect anything *wrong*, it just never saw HS traffic.

So the break is **at the D-PHY RX level** — the SAM9X75 D-PHY isn't acquiring the incoming CSI-2 high-speed signal from the TC358743 (which we know is transmitting). Either:

1. D-PHY config is wrong (bit-rate code, termination, calibration values), OR
2. The D-PHY-related init hasn't run the right sequence, OR
3. Some electrical issue (less likely given cable worked for you before).

Let me check the CSI_PHY_RX bit 16 meaning quickly, then ask for your patches.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 18:52:07Z)**_

Clear diagnosis: `CSI_PHY_RX = 0x00010000` has only bit 16 set (clock lane NOT in ULP = awake). Bit 17 (`PHY_RXCLKACTIVEHS` = "D-PHY clock lane is receiving DDR clock") is **0**. The PHY is awake but **never sees an HS clock**.

So the issue is: SAM9X75's D-PHY clock-lane side is not detecting TC358743's CSI-2 clock signal at all. TC358743's transmitting (TXACT=1), but the receive-side PHY is blind to it. This matches a configuration issue at the DWC D-PHY test-code level — analog config that tells the PHY how to look for the signal.

Perfect time to pull in your patches — they almost certainly address exactly this. Can you share them? Options:

- If they're in git commits (even on a branch that's not this repo), give me the commit hash(es) and which repo, or paste the diff here.
- If they're loose diffs or notes on what changed, paste them.

Once I see them I'll apply, then re-flash and re-read the diag dump — bit 17 (`PHY_RXCLKACTIVEHS`) flipping to 1 will be the key signal.

 static DRV_CSI2DC_OBJ csi2dcObj;
 
+/* Diagnostic accumulators populated by CSI2DC_Handler.
+ *
+ * Background: GISR is read-and-clear, so any one-shot snapshot of GISR
+ * loses transient bits that fired and were cleared by the ISR before
+ * we read it. We need *cumulative* counts of:
+ *   - SSP (Sync Short Packet, bit 0): every FS or FE the bridge emits
+ *   - SEC (Single-bit ECC corrected, bit 6): minor PHY-level corruption
+ *   - DED (Double-bit ECC detected,  bit 7): packet-killing corruption
+ *
+ * The bridge sends 1 FS + 1 FE per frame (60 Hz on our 720x480p60
+ * source) so SSP should clock at 120 Hz when streaming is healthy.
+ * SSP=0 over a 1-second window with GIER.SSP enabled => the bridge
+ * is NOT emitting short packets at all - that's the failure mode
+ * we've been chasing.
+ *
+ * Histogram registers: incremented in the ISR (which runs in a
+ * deferred context but at higher priority than main loop), read
+ * un-locked from main loop - we only need approximate counts so a
+ * race that drops one increment per million is fine.
+ */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcSspCount;   /* short sync (FS/FE) seen */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcSecCount;   /* single-bit ECC corrected */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcDedCount;   /* double-bit ECC detected */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcLastGisr;   /* most recent GISR snapshot */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcIsrCount;   /* total IRQ entries */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcVpCapCount; /* video-pipe CAPTURE events */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcVpErrCount; /* video-pipe RATEOVF | CTLOVF | STE */
+static volatile uint32_t gCsi2dcLastVpisr;  /* most recent VPISR snapshot */
+
 void CSI2DC_Handler(void) {
-    CSI2DC_Interrupt_Status();
-    //Todo handle register callbacks.
+    /* The CSI2DC IRQ to AIC is the OR of GISR-enabled bits, the
+     * VPISR-enabled bits, and the DPISR-enabled bits. The AIC line is
+     * level-sensitive (see plib_aic.c), so EVERY enabled latched bit
+     * must be drained inside this handler or the line stays high and
+     * the handler re-fires (or the AIC masks us off as runaway).
+     *
+     * `DRV_CSI2DC_Configure_VideoPipe()` enables:
+     *   GIER  : SSP | SEC | DED
+     *   VPIER : CAPTURE

+     *   DPIER : CAPTURE - we don't drain it here because the data pipe

TC358743 PLL: drop from 594 Mbps → 297 Mbps (FBD 88 → 44).** The comment in the working `drv_csi.c` explicitly calls this out: *"v13 (current, Test W): 0x14 (270-299) paired with bridge PLL at 297 Mbps/lane (FBD=44, FRS=1), a calibrated standard point."* Our HSFREQRANGE=0x14 is designed for 270-299 Mbps band — mismatched to our 594 Mbps. +     *
+     * The TC358743 HDMI-to-CSI bridge sources the CSI clock; this register
+     * only tells the SAM9X75 D-PHY receiver which frequency band to expect.
+     * It MUST match the rate the TC358743 is actually transmitting at,
+     * which is set by the TC358743_PLL_PRD/FBD/FRS macros in tc358743.c.
+     *
+     * --- Why 0x14 (v13 / Test W) ---
+     *

+     * tc358743.c). 297 falls in the 270-299 Mbps band, which the
+     * SAM9X75 D-PHY HSFREQRANGE table encodes as 0x14.
+     *
+     * --- Lookup (see disabled CSI_BitRateLookUp[] above) ---
+     *     0x05 -> 300-329 Mbps/lane
+     *     0x14 -> 270-299 Mbps/lane   <-- THIS, paired with 297 Mbps PLL
+     *     0x15 -> 330-359 Mbps/lane
+     *     0x25 -> 360-399 Mbps/lane   (Test T-safe; refuted - PHY ECC tripled)
+     *     0x06 -> 400-449 Mbps/lane
+     *     0x16 -> 450-499 Mbps/lane
+     *     0x07 -> 500-549 Mbps/lane
+     *     0x17 -> 550-599 Mbps/lane
+     *     0x08 -> 600-649 Mbps/lane
+     *     0x19 -> 750-799 Mbps/lane
+     *
+     * --- History ---
+     *   IMX219 era: 0x16 (450-499 Mbps), tuned for RAW10 720p.

+     * Future: if you change TC358743_PLL_FBD, RECOMPUTE this. The

static bool tc358743_set_pll(DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_OBJ* s)
{
    /* PLLCTL0 is purely PRD/FBD - we OWN the whole register, full overwrite. */
    uint16_t pllctl0 = (uint16_t)
        ((((uint32_t) TC358743_PLL_PRD - 1U) << PLLCTL0_PRD_SHIFT) & PLLCTL0_PRD_MASK)
      |  (((uint32_t) TC358743_PLL_FBD - 1U)                       & PLLCTL0_FBD_MASK);

    /* PLLCTL1: bits we touch, and the values we want them at. */
    const uint16_t mask_we_touch =
        (uint16_t)(PLLCTL1_FRS_MASK | PLLCTL1_RESETB | PLLCTL1_PLL_EN);
    const uint16_t pllctl1_enabled_bits = (uint16_t)
        (((((uint32_t) TC358743_PLL_FRS) << PLLCTL1_FRS_SHIFT) & PLLCTL1_FRS_MASK)
         | PLLCTL1_RESETB | PLLCTL1_PLL_EN);

    /* Bracket: enter sleep mode so chip clock domain is gated during
     * PLL re-programming. Matches upstream. */
    if (!tc358743_sleep_mode(s, true)) return false;

    /* Step 1: write PRD/FBD. */
    if (!tc358743_w16(s, REG_PLLCTL0, pllctl0)) return false;

    /* Step 2: RMW PLLCTL1 to set FRS/RESETB/PLL_EN while preserving
     * LBWS, BYPCKEN, CKEN-state, and any other bits the chip wants
     * left at their reset defaults. */
    {
        uint16_t v = 0U;
        if (!tc358743_r16(s, REG_PLLCTL1, &v)) return false;
        v = (uint16_t)((v & ~mask_we_touch) | pllctl1_enabled_bits);
        if (!tc358743_w16(s, REG_PLLCTL1, v)) return false;
    }

    tc358743_msleep(1);   /* let PLL lock; spec says <500 us, upstream uses 10 us */

    /* Step 3: RMW PLLCTL1 to set CKEN (ungate the PLL output clock),
     * preserving everything else (FRS/RESETB/PLL_EN/LBWS/...). */
    {
        uint16_t v = 0U;
        if (!tc358743_r16(s, REG_PLLCTL1, &v)) return false;
        v = (uint16_t)(v | PLLCTL1_CKEN);
        if (!tc358743_w16(s, REG_PLLCTL1, v)) return false;
    }

    /* Bracket: leave sleep mode so the freshly-locked PLL clock starts
     * driving downstream blocks. Matches upstream. */
    if (!tc358743_sleep_mode(s, false)) return false;

    debug_print("\r\n\t TC358743: PLL configured PRD=%u FBD=%u FRS=%u\r\n",
                TC358743_PLL_PRD, TC358743_PLL_FBD, TC358743_PLL_FRS);
    return true;
}

/* Phase 3: CSI-Tx D-PHY timing + lane configuration.
 *
 * Sequencing matches upstream Linux drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c
 * tc358743_set_csi() exactly. The order is load-bearing:
 *
 *   1.  Pulse SYSCTL.CTXRST so CSI_CONTROL and the CSI-Tx FSM start
 *       from a known-zero state. Without this, our CONFW SET-mode
 *       writes can only OR bits in - and the chip's reset-default
 *       value of CSI_CONTROL has bits we don't want (e.g. NOL=4-lane
 *       and a few reserved bits in the high byte) which we cannot
 *       clear via SET. Symptom: CSI_CONTROL reads back 0xBE00 with
 *       CSI_MODE forced on but TXHSMD/NOL_2 never sticking.
 *   2.  Lane enables / disables.
 *   3.  D-PHY timing counters.
 *   4.  HSTXVREGEN.
 *   5.  TXOPTIONCNTRL = continuous-clock mode (the LP-11->HS dance
 *       in enable_stream() will toggle this 0->1 again).
 *   6.  STARTCNTRL.START = 1, CSI_START.STRT = 1   (kick the PPI).
 *   7.  CSI_CONFW SET CSI_CONTROL = CSI_MODE | TXHSMD | NOL_2 .
 *   8.  Enable error/halt interrupts via additional CONFW writes,
 *       matching upstream so the chip's internal state-machine
 *       progresses past PHY init.
 *
 * Step 7's MASK_CSI_MODE (bit15=0x8000) is the bit we were missing
 * before; without it the CSI-Tx core stays in some non-CSI default,
 * which is exactly the "lanes never transmit, ARSTIP stuck" failure
 * we were chasing.
 */
static bool tc358743_set_csi_tx(DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_OBJ* s)
{
    /* Step 1: pulse CTXRST in SYSCTL to clear CSI-Tx state. This MUST
     * be a read-modify-write pulse, NOT a blind write, mirroring
     * upstream's tc358743_reset(sd, MASK_CTXRST):
     *
     *     v = i2c_rd16(SYSCTL);
     *     i2c_wr16(SYSCTL, v |  MASK_CTXRST);   // assert
     *     i2c_wr16(SYSCTL, v & ~MASK_CTXRST);   // deassert (using ORIGINAL v)
     *
     * A blind write would clobber IRRST/CECRST (which sw_reset() left
     * asserted on purpose) and accidentally release the IR/CEC engines
     * to run with uninitialised dividers — they share an internal
     * arbiter with CSI-Tx and can wedge it.
     */
    {
        uint16_t v = 0U;
        if (!tc358743_r16(s, REG_SYSCTL, &v)) return false;
        if (!tc358743_w16(s, REG_SYSCTL,
                          (uint16_t)(v | SYSCTL_CTXRST))) return false;
        tc358743_msleep(1);
        if (!tc358743_w16(s, REG_SYSCTL,
                          (uint16_t)(v & ~SYSCTL_CTXRST))) return false;
        tc358743_msleep(1);
    }

    /* Step 1b: program FIFOCTL with the upstream-canonical drain
     * threshold (374 half-words). See the FIFOCTL_DEFAULT comment
     * near the register definition for the full bandwidth reasoning. */
    if (!tc358743_w16(s, REG_FIFOCTL, FIFOCTL_DEFAULT)) return false;

    /* Step 2: lane enables. Bit0=0 enables, bit0=1 disables. */
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_CLW_CNTRL, LANE_ENABLE))  return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_D0W_CNTRL, LANE_ENABLE))  return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_D1W_CNTRL,
                      (TC358743_NUM_LANES >= 2U) ? LANE_ENABLE : LANE_DISABLE)) return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_D2W_CNTRL, LANE_DISABLE)) return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_D3W_CNTRL, LANE_DISABLE)) return false;

    /* Step 3: D-PHY timing counters (TC358743_* values defined at top). */
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_LINEINITCNT,    TC358743_LINEINITCNT))    return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_LPTXTIMECNT,    TC358743_LPTXTIMECNT))    return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_TCLK_HEADERCNT, TC358743_TCLK_HEADERCNT)) return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_TCLK_TRAILCNT,  TC358743_TCLK_TRAILCNT))  return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_THS_HEADERCNT,  TC358743_THS_HEADERCNT))  return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_TWAKEUP,        TC358743_TWAKEUP))        return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_TCLK_POSTCNT,   TC358743_TCLK_POSTCNT))   return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_THS_TRAILCNT,   TC358743_THS_TRAILCNT))   return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_HSTXVREGCNT,    TC358743_HSTXVREGCNT))    return false;

    /* Step 4: HS voltage regulator on clock + D0 + D1 (CLM | D0M | D1M). */
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_HSTXVREGEN, 0x00000007U)) return false;

    /* Step 5: continuous-clock mode (TXOPTIONCNTRL = CONTCLKMODE).
     *
     * Matches upstream Linux's tc358743_set_csi():
     *   i2c_wr32(sd, TXOPTIONCNTRL, MASK_CONTCLKMODE);
     *
     * tc358743_start() will then pulse TXOPTIONCNTRL 0 -> CONTCLKMODE
     * again to drive the documented LP-11 -> HS edge on the clock lane
     * that the host D-PHY needs to lock its byte clock.
     *
     * Invariant: this MUST stay in sync with the descriptor's
     * .csiContinuousClock=true (camera layer programs CSI2DC.MIPIFRN=0
     * = free-running) AND with the tc358743_start() pulse. Mismatched
     * bridge/host clock modes leave CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP stuck. */
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_TXOPTIONCNTRL, TXOPTIONCNTRL_CONTCLKMODE)) return false;

    /* Step 6: kick the PPI / streaming state machines. Both bits are
     * "kick" bits and self-clear when the chip accepts them. */
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_STARTCNTRL, STARTCNTRL_START)) return false;
    if (!tc358743_w32(s, REG_CSI_START,  CSI_START_STRT))   return false;

    /* Step 7: configure CSI_CONTROL via the indirect CONFW path.
     *
     * SET-only, no CLR pass — matches upstream Linux's
     * enable_stream(): whatever bits are in the chip's startup
     * CSI_CONTROL stay there, we OR in {CSI_MODE | TXHSMD | NOL_*}.
     *
     * Documented bit map per upstream tc358743_regs.h:
     *   bit15  CSI_MODE   0x8000  -> we SET
     *   bit10  HTXTOEN    0x0400  -> leave at chip default
     *   bit7   TXHSMD     0x0080  -> we SET
```

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 19:02:40Z)**_

**Found the issue.** `CSI2DC_GSR = 0x02` means bit 1 (`ARSTIP`) is set — **Asynchronous Reset In Progress** is stuck. This matches a comment in the emirror working code:

> *Mismatched bridge/host clock modes leave CSI2DC.GSR.ARSTIP stuck.*

The async-reset gets stuck when TC358743's continuous-clock mode doesn't match CSI2DC's MIPIFRN (MIPI Free-Running) setting. Let me check our MIPIFRN config.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 19:03:02Z)**_

Got it. **`CSI2DC_ENABLE_MIPI_CLOCK_FREE_RUN = false` is wrong for our TC358743 continuous-clock setup.** MCC defaulted it to `false`, meaning CSI2DC is in gated-clock mode — but TC358743 emits continuous clock (TXOPTIONCNTRL = CONTCLKMODE), and the mismatch locks ARSTIP.

Fix: override `enableMIPIFreeRun = true` in our [isc_capture.c](firmware/marvin/default/src/isc_capture.c). Same pattern as the `csiBitRate` override — leaves MCC defaults untouched.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 19:07:57Z)**_

Found the real issue — **ordering**. Emirror's working flow configures CSI-RX (and CSI2DC and ISC) **before** enabling TC358743's stream. We're doing the opposite — TC358743 starts transmitting, then we configure CSI-RX. The CSI-RX D-PHY misses the LP11→HS edge that the TC358743's `TXOPTIONCNTRL 0→CONTCLKMODE` toggle produces, because CSI-RX is in reset at that instant.

Emirror's sequence:

```
CAMERA_Open:
    DRV_CSI2DC_Configure()   ← RX side ready first
    DRV_CSI_Configure()
    DRV_ISC_Configure()

CAMERA_Start_Capture:
    DRV_ImageSensor_Start()  ← then source starts transmitting
    DRV_ISC_Start_Capture()  ← then ISC arms + polls VD
```

Our current flow has TC358743 auto-starting its stream on SYNC lock (inside its watcher), then later the app asks ISC to configure+start. Need to restructure.

**Plan:**

1. Split `ISC_Capture_Start(w, h)` → `ISC_Capture_Configure(w, h)` + `ISC_Capture_Start()`.
2. Expose `TC358743_EnableStream(bool)` publicly; remove auto-stream-toggle from the tc358743 watcher.
3. `app.c` orchestrates in order: Configure → EnableStream(true) → Start.
4. Flip configure order to CSI2DC → CSI → ISC (matches emirror).

Implementing now.

Changes applied. Summary of all Phase 5 fixes so far:

| # | Fix | Where |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | TC358743 PLL 594 → 297 Mbps/lane | tc358743.c |
| 2 | CSI2DC VPCFGR.RMS = 1 (byte stream) | plib_csi2dc.c |
| 3 | MIPIFRN = 0 (free-running, matches cont-clock) | isc_capture.c |
| 4 | **Order: Configure RX → EnableStream → Start** | app.c + refactor |

The big architectural change this round:

- `tc358743.c` watcher no longer enables/disables the stream automatically.
- New public API `TC358743_EnableStream(bool)`.
- `ISC_Capture_Start(w,h)` split into `ISC_Capture_Configure(w,h)` + `ISC_Capture_Start()`.
- `app.c` orchestrates: Configure → EnableStream → Start.
- Configure order flipped to CSI2DC → CSI → ISC (matches emirror).

Expected output on flash:

```
TC358743: detected 720x480p @ 60 Hz, RGB limited-range
ISC_Capture: configured 720x480 ARGB32 (...)
ISC_Capture diag (pre-start):
  ...
  CSI2DC_GSR=0x00000000       ← ARSTIP cleared
  CSI2DC_FNVC0R=...>0         ← frames arriving
ISC_Capture: capture started
ISC: ~60 fps
```

If `CSI2DC_GSR=0x02` persists despite the order change, something else is keeping async reset stuck and we'll need yet another fix. Flash and share.

I have enough. Let me produce the report.

---

## Debug journal report — TC358743 + SAM9X75 CSI-2 bring-up

**1. Load-bearing fixes beyond your list**

- **Lane-1 HSFREQRANGE write is critical and has a subtle auto-increment mechanic** (Test O, lines 1863-1948). The Synopsys D-PHY auto-increments test-register address after each `TESTEN=0` write. Lane-0's 3-write sequence is `TESTEN=1 select`, `TESTEN=0 0x94`, `TESTEN=0 bit_rate`. The lane-1 block in upstream `CSI_Analog_Init()` had only the first two — the `bit_rate` write was missing. You say you applied this; double-check that in your `plib_csi.c` the lane-1 path writes all three beats in that exact order (select 0x54, then 0x94, then `bit_rate`). Journal calls out that lane-2 and lane-3 blocks in the MCC code also have the missing write plus a `TESTDIN(0x24)` typo (comment says 0x64) — irrelevant here but confirms the code's PHY init is buggy by default.
- **Enable CSI2DC interrupts:** `SYS_INT_SourceEnable(ID_CSI2DC)` was never called in the original port (line 659, 627-629). Without it, `csi2dc{ssp/sec/ded/isr}` counters stay zero even when VPISR fires. This is diagnostic, not load-bearing, but it matters while you're debugging ARSTIP because you need CSI2DC visibility.
- **`CSI_STATUS` `+TXACT` sampling is unreliable** (line 631-635, 673). Single-shot reads catch LP-11 idle between line packets — you cannot use one-shot TXACT to argue "bridge silent." Use the tight-loop "ever saw TXACT in window" form from the Test-S `tc358743_start_csi_timeline()` instrumentation (line 2305).
- **FIFOCTL = 0x0176** (journal §2/line 440). Verify in your binary dump that `FIFOCTL = 0x0176` and `TXOPTCNTRL = 0x00000001`. The source was drifted to 0x0300 at one point (line 669) and the revert was never committed.

**2. ARSTIP-stuck observations**

Directly addressed at **O4 (lines 297-310)**. The journal never *resolved* what `CSI2DC.GSR=0x02` means — it's labelled "ARSTIP" inferentially without datasheet confirmation. The recommended action was to investigate D-PHY PPI counters: `LINEINIT`, `LPTXTIME`, `TCLK_HDR`, `TCLK_POST`, `THS_HDR`, `TWAKEUP`, `HSTXVREGEN`, `HSTXVREGC`. Test R's crash dump (lines 2620-2632) lists the actual values programmed on the **bridge** side — these are TC358743 regs, not host D-PHY, but the implication is they're computed per-bitrate and can be wrong. In the journal's case, ARSTIP cleared "eventually" in the working 297 Mbps path — no register fix was ever explicitly documented as the ARSTIP unblocker.

**3. PHY-level config you might have missed**

- **HSFREQRANGE write on lane 0 AND lane 1**, using the auto-increment path described above (Test O).
- **Synopsys D-PHY test-code interface:** journal notes at line 1934-1936 that the auto-increment assumption *might* be wrong and a future fix may need an explicit `0x55` select before the HSFREQRANGE write on lane 1 (lane 1 HS RX Control B). If your ARSTIP is stuck after applying the Test O fix, this is worth trying.
- The journal did *not* audit SAM9X75 CSI reset/shutdown ordering explicitly. If your port builds `DRV_CSI_Configure()` → `CSI_Analog_Init()` → `CSI_Configure_Lane()` in a different order than the `emirror` copy, inspect that.

**4. TC358743 gotchas for CSI-RX lock**

- **Bring-up order:** upstream does `set_ref_clk → init_hdmi → load_edid → set_pll → set_csi_tx`, not the other way around (O8, lines 331-354; Test U lines 2743-2788). Test U alone was refuted as sufficient but the ordering stayed in the final baseline.
- **ANA_CTL = 0x31** must be re-asserted after the chip enters DVI mode (H5, line 239). **VI_MUTE = 0xC0** (MASK_AUTO_MUTE) per upstream (H4, line 238). Both are clobbered in some reset paths.
- **Do not pulse `SYSCTL.CTXRST`** without a full re-config — Test R (lines 2611-2645) showed CTXRST wipes LINEINIT/LPTXTIME/TCLK_HDR/TWAKEUP/TCLK_POST/HSTXVREGEN/HSTXVREGC/CSI_CONTROL/D2W_CNTRL/D3W_CNTRL/CSI_INT_ENA/CSI_ERR_INTENA/CSI_ERR_HALT to chip defaults, leaving 4 lanes "enabled" and HALT armed on every error.
- **LP-11 → HS pulse on `TXOPTIONCNTRL`:** `TXOPTIONCNTRL = 0; TXOPTIONCNTRL = CONTCLKMODE` in `start()` (H3, line 237) — kept in final code.
- **EDID with CEA-861 extension** advertising HDMI (Q5 / Test L) — not load-bearing for the ARSTIP you're hitting, but affects which internal bridge FSM runs.

**5. "It finally worked" moment**

**Test W (lines 2837-2885):** single-variable change from 594 → 297 Mbps/lane paired with host `csiBitRate=0x14` (270-299 band). PLL: PRD=4, **FBD=44, FRS=1**. Preceded by Test V (remove STARTCNTRL/CSI_START re-kick at step 4 to match upstream `enable_stream(true)` — no `STARTCNTRL_START`/`CSI_START_STRT` writes in start; step-4 snapshot kept as marker only) and Test U (Linux-order configure sequencing). Test W alone was what flipped it to stable 60 fps, `VPISR=0x01` only, `sec=0 ded=0`. Confirm your start() does NOT re-kick STARTCNTRL/CSI_START after VBUFEN — if you're still doing that it matches Test V's pre-fix failure mode where `+TXACT @ step3` collapsed to `-TXACT @ step4`.

**Specific values to double-check in your port**

- `plib_csi.c::CSI_Analog_Init()` lane-1 path writes 3 transactions (select 0x54, 0x94, `bit_rate=0x14`) — not 2.
- `FIFOCTL = 0x0176`, `TXOPTCNTRL = 0x00000001` in binary readback.
- `TC358743_PLL_PRD=4, FBD=44, FRS=1`.
- `csiObj.csiBitRate = 0x14`.
- `tc358743_start()` does *not* write `REG_STARTCNTRL`/`REG_CSI_START` (no step-4 re-kick).
- `tc358743_configure()` order: `reset → set_ref_clk → init_hdmi → load_edid → set_pll → set_csi_tx`.
- `CSI_CONTROL` programmed SET-only, not CLR-then-SET (line 674, Test B at lines 864-893). The CLR pass spuriously triggered an early HS burst at VBUFEN; upstream SET-only is cleaner.
- After `CSI_Analog_Init()`, read back `CSI.PUSR` and `CSI_PCR`/`PMR` (O7, line 375) — the journal never got around to doing this and recommended it for 1-lane debug; same value in tracking ARSTIP stuck is worth the read.
- `ISC` input config — `ISC_INPUT_FORMAT_TYPE=RGB`, `ISC_INPUT_BIT_WIDTH=8_BIT`, `ISC_OUTPUT_FORMAT_TYPE=ARGB32`, `ISC_OUTPUT_LAYOUT_TYPE=PACKED32`, `CSI_DATA_FORMAT_TYPE=RGB888` (line 570-580).

332

337	`tc358743_init_hdmi()` (see `tc358743.c:2685-2692`). Programming the CSI

339	CSI-Tx FSM in a state where it has been "started" but the upstream

2401	    >  (using 2 lanes) and 1080p60 (using 4 lanes), but FAILS when

2409	**H7j: the FIFO underruns mid-line**
2410	
2411	  When the bridge starts a CSI long-packet burst, drain is faster
2412	  than fill, so within a single line the FIFO can go dry. The
2413	  bridge then either:
2414	    (a) emits a TRUNCATED long packet whose CRC happens to pass
2415	        by random chance -> host accepts it as a valid frame
2416	        (corrupt pixels but the host doesn't notice yet) -> we
2417	        run at 60 fps with garbage data.
2418	    (b) emits a truncated long packet whose CRC doesn't pass /
2419	        whose word count is wrong -> host's CSI2DC raises STE
2420	        (Start Token Error) and CTLOVF -> the line is dropped,
2421	        VDTO eventually fires -> 5 fps mode.
2422	    (c) eventually a "good" 60-fps boot drifts into mode (b) when
2423	        a truncation happens with bad CRC -> VDTO -> freeze.
2424	
2425	  All three modes are observed in our 4 boots. **Mode (c) unifies
2426	  the freeze with the fps split: it's the same bug, observed at
2427	  different timescales.**
2428	
2429	  Symptom-to-mechanism crosswalk:
2430	
2431	  | Symptom | H7j explanation |
2432	  |---|---|
2433	  | VPISR=0x0D (+CAP +CTLOVF +STE) in 5-fps mode | truncated long packets with bad CRC |
2434	  | VPISR=0x2D (adds RATEOVF) when degrading | host sees byte-count vs. clock ratio mismatch |
2435	  | Identical pre-Start dump for 60 vs 5 boots | bug is per-line, not per-boot - depends on luck |
2436	  | SYS_STATUS, ANA_CTL stable | failure is on the CSI-Tx side, HDMI side is fine |
2437	  | 60-fps boots eventually freeze (boots 1, 4) | each line is a CRC dice roll; eventually one fails badly |
2438	  | FIFOCTL = 0x0176 doesn't help | no threshold can rescue drain > fill |
2439	
2440	**Why didn't this manifest at 1-lane?** At 1-lane, drain=594 vs
2441	fill=648. Drain is LESS than fill, so the bridge cannot underrun
2442	mid-line - instead the FIFO grows and the bridge drops whole
2443	frames cleanly via its internal frame-skip logic, giving a stable
2444	~5 fps with no STE/CTLOVF errors. The prior 1-lane testing logs
2445	match this exactly (Test N: "vpisr=0x0D(+CAP)" was actually +CAP
2446	alone in those traces; the persistent CTLOVF+STE we see now at
2447	2-lane was new with 2-lane). [TODO: spot-check that claim against
2448	Test N log when we revisit; if the 1-lane log also showed
2449	STE+CTLOVF, then the H7j model needs another cycle of refinement.]
2450	
2451	**Why does upstream's 374 work for upstream's tested cases?**
2452	Upstream tests at 720p60 (1280x720, pixel clock 74.25 MHz, fill
2453	1782 Mbps) and 1080p60 (4-lane). Both have fill >= drain. They
2454	are NEVER in the drain-exceeds-fill regime. Our 720x480 with the
2455	same upstream PLL setting puts us in territory upstream
2456	explicitly says "FAILS".
2457

2537	## Cycle: Test R (IMPLEMENTED, awaits flash) - HDMIRST+CTXRST pulse with selective restore
2538	
2539	Hypothesis:  H7i revisited (not H7j). The random 60-vs-5 fps boot
2540	             split at 594 Mbps/lane is a START-UP PHASE RACE
2541	             between the bridge's CSI-Tx FSM and the HDMI receive
2542	             FIFO. When our STARTCNTRL/CSI_START writes happen at
2543	             a "good" phase relative to HDMI vsync, the FIFO and
2544	             FSM align and the host sees a clean FS short packet
2545	             on its first poll (boots that ran at 60 fps in v10
2546	             and at 12-19 fps in v11). When they happen at a
2547	             "bad" phase, the FIFO and FSM are misaligned and
2548	             the host sees no FS for 100-700 polls
2549	             (5 fps in v10, 1-2 fps in v11). Pulsing HDMIRST +
2550	             CTXRST TOGETHER, then restoring the four front-end
2551	             registers HDMIRST is known to clobber, then running
2552	             the regular start sequence, forces both blocks out
2553	             of reset on the same edge - eliminating the race.
2554	Predicted:   - 60 fps stable, 100% of boots (or at minimum,
2555	               significantly tighter distribution than 50/50
2556	               60-vs-5)
2557	             - VD seen by ISC_Drv_Start_Capture on the first or
2558	               second poll EVERY boot (was 1 poll on lucky
2559	               boots, 100-700 on unlucky)
2560	             - VPISR=0x01 (+CAP only) sustained, no CTLOVF / STE
2561	               in steady state
2562	             - csi2dc{sec, ded} should DROP back to ~16/16
2563	               per ~5 M loops (back to the v10 PHY noise floor)
2564	             - SYS_STATUS post-pulse logs SYNC re-establishing
2565	               in <100 ms (bridge re-locks to live HDMI source)
2566	             - The four restored front-end registers (ANA_CTL,
2567	               VI_MODE, VOUT_SET2, VOUT_SET3) read back at their
2568	               configure() values in the post-Start dump
2569	             - If still split: H7i is also wrong; back to first
2570	               principles and consider host-side DMA / CSI2DC
2571	               state-machine bugs (Q7-freeze H7b becomes primary).
2572	             - If 60-fps stable but freezes return after long
2573	               run: Q7-freeze is independent (H7b host-side DMA
2574	               exhaustion) and we tackle it separately.

2583	         values tc358743_init_hdmi() set originally.

2589	       Update FIFOCTL HISTORY / PLL HISTORY comment blocks
2590	         with v12 entry documenting Test R.

2593	       Update comment block accordingly.

1882	incompatible with the bridge's 594 Mbps output. Lane 0 deserialised
