456	> **Original D16 results, kept here for reference.** D15's flash log
457	> confirmed the burst-size change landed (`ISC_DCFG = 0x00000022`,
458	> decoded `IMODE=PACKED32 YMBSIZE=BEATS8 CMBSIZE=0`) but every
459	> visible symptom was unchanged from D14: framebuffer showed
460	> `[XX 00 00 00]` per 4-byte slot, HDTO still fired
461	> (`ISC_INTSR = 0x08000002`), display all-blue at ~2/3
462	> vertical height. **The AHB-back-pressure hypothesis was
463	> rejected** by D15.
464	>
465	> Cross-check against Linux confirmed the disproof: our
466	> register programming after D13+D15 is byte-for-byte
467	> identical to `microchip-isc-base.c::isc_set_pipeline()`'s
468	> mapping for `V4L2_PIX_FMT_UYVY` plus
469	> `microchip-sama5d2-isc.c::isc_sama5d2_config_rlp()`'s
470	> YCYC->YYCC remap. We are matching a known-working Linux
471	> classic-ISC config and still getting `[XX 00 00 00]` byte
472	> cadence. The byte loss is not in MODE/YMODE/IMODE/YMBSIZE.
473	>
474	> The byte-loss cadence is also invariant across every
475	> YUV-pipeline knob we own: it survived D11 (`PACKED16`),
476	> D12 (`PACKED32 + YMODE=UYVY`), D13 (`MODE=YYCC`), and D15
477	> (`YMBSIZE=BEATS8`). That insensitivity is a strong signal
478	> the missing 3 bytes per 4-byte slot are dropped **upstream
479	> of the RLP**, not by the RLP/DMA pair. The two chain
480	> elements our setup has that Linux's working sama5d2 path
481	> does *not* are (a) `ISC_PFE_CFG0.MIPI = 1` and
482	> (b) the CSI2DC sitting between MIPI and the PFE.
483	>
484	> **D16 change — diagnostic, not a fix.** Pivot the entire
485	> RLP+DMA stage to the simplest possible path
486	> (Linux's `V4L2_PIX_FMT_GREY` mapping):
487	>
488	> 1. `configuration.h`:
489	>    `ISC_OUTPUT_FORMAT_TYPE = ISC_RLP_CFG_MODE_DAT8`,
490	>    `ISC_OUTPUT_LAYOUT_TYPE = ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED8`.
491	> 2. `drv_isc.c`: no code change. The D12/D13 YMODE-override
492	>    is gated on `MODE_YYCC`, so it self-disables under
493	>    DAT8 and re-enables on revert. Comment block expanded
494	>    to document this.
495	> 3. Banners bumped to `D16=PACKED8+DAT8`.
496	> 4. Dump-line "want" hints updated:
497	>    `ISC_RLP_CFG` -> `MODE=DAT8` (YMODE irrelevant);
498	>    `ISC_DCFG` -> `0x00000020` (`IMODE=PACKED8 YMBSIZE=BEATS8`).
499	>
500	> **The displayed image will be garbage** — HEO is still in
501	> 16bpp RGB565 and is now reading raw YUV bytes as RGB565.
502	> That is expected. The diagnostic signal is the byte cadence
503	> in `heofb snap`, not the pixels on screen.
504	>
505	> **D15's `YMBSIZE_BEATS8` is preserved** via the `else`
506	> branch in `DRV_ISC_Configure_DMA` (which is the branch
507	> `LAYOUT_PACKED8` falls into). All other bridge/CSI2DC/PFE
508	> registers are unchanged.
509	>
510	> **Frame-slot size halves** (8bpp instead of 16bpp), so each
511	> DMA frame slot is 720×480×1 = 345,600 B. Two slots fit in
512	> the same `GBuffer` region. The snapshot tool's row stride
513	> stays at 1440 B (16bpp assumption), so it samples DMA
514	> rows `0, 2, 4, 6, 16, 128, 256, 480, 640, 800, 958` —
515	> still useful for byte-cadence analysis.
516	>
517	> **What to look for in the next boot log:**
518	>
519	> | Dump line | Expected D16 value | Meaning if different |
520	> |---|---|---|
521	> | `ISC_RLP_CFG  = 0x____FF08` | `MODE=0x8 DAT8` | If MODE != 0x8, configuration.h didn't land. Check the `ISC_OUTPUT_FORMAT_TYPE` macro. |
522	> | `ISC_DCFG    = 0x00000020` | `IMODE=0x0 PACKED8, YMBSIZE=0x2 BEATS8, CMBSIZE=0x0` | If IMODE != 0x0, the layout switch didn't land. Check `ISC_OUTPUT_LAYOUT_TYPE`. |
523	>
524	> | Snapshot window pattern after D16 | Implication | Next experiment (D17) |
525	> |---|---|---|
526	> | `XX YY ZZ AA BB CC DD EE ...` (every byte populated, varying smoothly — looks like a UYVY byte stream from the bridge) | ✓ The PFE/DMA chain is healthy. The byte loss came from the RLP YYCC packing rule somehow malforming output despite matching Linux. | Restore `MODE=YYCC + IMODE=PACKED32` but investigate why YYCC's byte-pack collapses on `PFE.MIPI=1`: try `LSH` bit; verify Linux's CSC->RLP->DMA write order; check whether YYCC silently expects `PFE_CFG0.PPM` (parallel-pixel-mode), which is ignored in MIPI mode. |
527	> | `XX 00 00 00 XX 00 00 00 ...` (unchanged from D15) | ✗ Loss is upstream of the RLP. PFE delivers ~1 sample per 4 ISC clocks, OR CSI2DC asserts `valid` only every 4th clock. | Two cheap follow-ups: (a) try `PFE_CFG0.MIPI = 0` for one boot to see if MIPI-mode timing path is the differential; (b) explicitly call `ISC_PFE_Crop_Area(0, W-1, 0, H-1)` — currently `PFE_CFG1/CFG2 = 0` may be interpreted as a zero-width window. |
528	> | `XX 00 XX 00 XX 00 ...` (every 2nd byte populated) | Half-rate from PFE or CSI2DC. | Compare CSI2DC vs ISC clock divisors; or try `MODE=DATY10` (forces 16-bit RLP word per sample). |
529	> | Memory mostly empty / `00 00 00 ...` | DMA isn't writing at all — check `LAYOUT_PACKED8` is in the `switch` covered branches (it is, line 165) and `ISC_CTRLSR` shows capture pending. |
530	> | HDTO clears under D16 (`ISC_INTSR & 0x08000000 == 0`) | RLP back-pressure was driving HDTO. PFE *can* keep up; YYCC packing is what backed up the RLP. | Important data point even if byte cadence is unchanged. |
531	> | HDTO still fires under D16 | HDTO is genuinely PFE/CSI2DC-side. RLP isn't backing up. | Combined with byte-cadence row above, nails the diagnosis as PFE/CSI2DC clock or sync. |

548	- Capture path (TC358743 -> CSI2DC -> ISC -> SDRAM) is **healthy
549	  at 60 fps**. All "blue static" / "blank screen" symptoms since
550	  D2 have been on the **display side** (HEO framebuffer
551	  contents, blend factors, byte order, layer ownership), not on
552	  the capture side. Don't go re-debugging the bridge.
553	- D3 fixed OVR1 byte order (the GUI logo / FPS / zoom are now
554	  the correct color).
555	- D4 fixed CPU-cache-vs-DMA tearing on the HEO test pattern by
556	  giving the test pattern a dedicated buffer in
557	  `.region_nocache` (`appTestPatternFb`, lands at `0x2002EE00`,
558	  MMU-mapped strongly-ordered).
559	- D5 explains why D4's HEO went **blank**: Legato installs
560	  a root widget on layer 0 (= canvas 0 = HEO). Even with
561	  `LE_WIDGET_BACKGROUND_NONE` the renderer still blits an
562	  800x480 zero-filled scratch tile into `canvas[0].pixelBuffer
563	  -> appTestPatternFb` on every `leUpdate(0)`, wiping our
564	  bands to opaque black. Workaround: re-run
565	  `APP_FillHEOTestPattern()` every frame (cheap because the
566	  buffer is non-cached). User confirms full color bars +
567	  GUI overlay rendering correctly post-D5.
568	- D6 flipped `APP_CAMERA_USE_TEST_PATTERN` back to `0` so HEO
569	  points at the live ISC `GBuffer` ring. Outcome: "flickering
570	  color bars with static blue in top half of screen" on a
571	  source the user reports as full-color / lots of white.
572	  `heofb snap` showed every sampled pixel as `0xFF0000XX` -
573	  alpha = our 0xFF override, B byte varying, R/G byte always 0.
574	  Idle loops/sec recovered to the expected hundreds-of-thousands
575	  range.
576	- D7 (this cycle) explains and fixes the `0xFF0000XX` pattern.
577	  Root cause: `ISC_PFE_CFG0.BPS` was being programmed to
578	  `EIGHT` for the TC358743 because the bridge driver reports
579	  `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT` (correct as a per-component width)
580	  and `drv_isc.c` used that value for BPS unconditionally. For
581	  *MIPI* sources BPS must be `FORTY` regardless of pixel depth
582	  (per the SAM9X75 manual: "FORTY: 40-bit input, used for MIPI
583	  formats up to forty bits per pixel"). With BPS=EIGHT + MIPI,
584	  the PFE sampler consumes only one byte per pixel period from
585	  the CSI2DC byte stream, dropping the other two bytes of every
586	  RGB888 pixel; the surviving byte gets packed into the B lane
587	  by the RLP, R/G stay at zero, and the alpha override fills
588	  in 0xFF - exactly the framebuffer we observed. Fix in
589	  `drv_isc.c`: branch on `enableMIPI` and force `BPS_FORTY`
590	  for MIPI sources; parallel sensors keep the legacy
591	  `4 - inputBits` mapping. Also corrected the misleading
592	  comment in `tc358743_get_config()` that claimed reporting
593	  `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT` would translate into BPS=EIGHT
594	  ("correct"), since that translation was the bug.
595	- D8 hypothesised that flipping `CSI2DC_POST_ALIGNED` to `true`
596	  (PA=1, MSB-aligned in each 12-bit ISC slot) would fix the
597	  residual missing-red channel post-D7. The flip was applied
598	  and confirmed by the register dump (`CSI2DC VPCFGR =
599	  0x00004024`), **but the framebuffer bit pattern did not
600	  change at all** — same nibble-stuck `0xFF00GGBB` signature
601	  with R always zero and the same `byte0 & 0xC1` /
602	  `byte1 & 0xF0` constants. So PA was *not* the cause of the
603	  channel-loss problem. PA=true is kept anyway because it
604	  matches the upstream Linux atmel-csi2dc convention for
605	  serial mode (see Cycle D9 for the source-of-truth
606	  reference) — it is harmless, and will be needed once the
607	  format is right.
608	- D9 (this cycle) is the structural-finding cycle. A direct
609	  review of the upstream Linux drivers — `microchip-sama7g5-
610	  isc.c` (`sama7g5_formats_list[]`) and `microchip-csi2dc.c`
611	  (`csi2dc_formats[]`) — shows that the SAM9X75 ISC pipeline
612	  has **no input format that matches 24bpp packed RGB888 over
613	  MIPI** (DT=0x24). The ISC PFE/RLP path supports at most
614	  2 bytes per pixel from MIPI: Bayer 8/10/12, GREY (Y8),
615	  YUYV/UYVY (YUV422 8-bit), RGB565, Y10. The CSI2DC similarly
616	  only knows DT=0x2A (RAW8), 0x2B (RAW10), 0x1E (YUV422_8B).
617	  No combination of `BPS`, `PA`, `RLP MODE` or any other PFE/
618	  RLP/CSI2DC tuning at the host can recover R when the
619	  upstream is delivering 3 bytes per pixel — there simply is
620	  no per-pixel grouping mode for it. This is why D7 (BPS) and
621	  D8 (PA) couldn't fix it.
622	- D9 actions:
623	    - **Reverted D7** in `drv_isc.c`. The unconditional
624	      `BPS_FORTY` for any MIPI source (a) contradicts Linux
625	      (which uses per-component BPS even for MIPI 2-byte/px
626	      formats), (b) silently regressed IMX219 (its 10-bit
627	      Bayer needs `BPS_TEN`, which D7 would have overridden),
628	      and (c) didn't actually fix TC358743. Restored the
629	      original `(4 - inputBits)` mapping with a long
630	      explanatory comment so the next agent doesn't try the
631	      same thing again.
632	    - Updated `tc358743.c` `tc358743_get_config()` comment to
633	      remove the misleading "BPS=FORTY for MIPI" claim and
634	      point at this D9 entry.
635	    - **Kept D8** (`CSI2DC_POST_ALIGNED = true`). Reframed
636	      the comment in `configuration.h` to explain that PA=1
637	      matches Linux's unconditional serial-mode behaviour,
638	      not specifically RGB888.
639	    - Updated the `ISC_OUTPUT_FORMAT_TYPE` comment in

641	      while we're (mistakenly) trying to ingest 24bpp RGB,

743	### Where we are
744	
745	- Link/capture baseline (Test W in main journal) is stable at ~60 fps.
746	- Display path is enabled in `app.c` (`APP_DISABLE_CAMERA_CALLBACK=0`),
747	  framebuffer sanity logging is enabled (`APP_FRAMEBUFFER_SANITY_LOG=1`).
748	- Bridge confirms `VI_STATUS3 = 0x00 (input=RGB, full range)` and
749	  `VOUT_SET2 = 0x01 (SEL422=0, CMODE=AUTO)` -> **source is RGB**, not
750	  YCbCr. YCbCr->RGB CSC mismatch hypothesis is **disproved**.
751	- D1 hypothesis (XSTRIDE underflow alone) is **disproved** by user
752	  observation: switching to ONE_TO_ONE layout produced "edge-to-edge
753	  top-half static" with the GUI overlay also showing as all-blue.
754	  Edge-to-edge contradicts the predicted pillarbox; "GUI also blue"
755	  promotes the failure beyond just the camera HEO layer.
756	- D2 fixes verified by register dump but did **not** clear the blue
757	  static. Both fixes still in place:
758	  1. `gfxcCanvasUpdate()` was resetting `LCDC_HEOCFG12` to MCC boot
759	     defaults (SFACTC=A0*Ad, DFACTC=1-A0*As) on every camera frame,
760	     undoing our explicit src-only blend. Fixed by re-applying
761	     `APP_ConfigureHEOForCameraFramebuffer()` after every canvas
762	     update; dump confirms `cfg12=0x00FF8283 sfactc=2 dfactc=0 a0=255`.
763	  2. ISC RLP packed `alpha = 0` into every framebuffer pixel
764	     (`drv_isc.c:447` passed `0` to `ISC_RLP_Configure`), making the
765	     framebuffer fully transparent under the boot-default blend.
766	     Fixed to write `0xFF`; dump confirms `ISC_RLP_CFG = 0x0000FF0A`.
767	- D3 leading hypothesis (applied):
768	  1. **OVR1 RGBMODE is wrong.** `XLCDC_SetupOVR1Layer()` (MCC) hard
769	     codes OVR1 `RGBMODE = 12 (ARGB_8888)` but `gfx_canvas_config.c`
770	     configures the GUI canvas as `RGBA_8888`, and Legato writes
771	     RGBA bytes. The driver IOCTL handlers don't propagate the
772	     canvas color mode to the OVR1 register. Result: a red
773	     Microchip logo pixel `(R,G,B,A)=(255,0,0,255)` is read by OVR1
774	     as `(B,G,R,A)=(255,0,0,255)` -> solid blue. Fixed in app by
775	     calling `XLCDC_SetLayerRGBColorMode(OVR1, RGBA_8888, ...)`
776	     once at init and after every camera-canvas update.
777	  2. **HEO byte order is unverified.** Same kind of mismatch may
778	     also exist between `ISC_RLP_CFG.MODE = ARGB32` and
779	     `LCDC_HEOCFG1.RGBMODE = ARGB_8888`. To prove it one way or
780	     the other, D3 introduces `APP_CAMERA_USE_TEST_PATTERN = 1`,
781	     which overwrites the just-completed ISC framebuffer with
782	     vertical bands of `black|red|green|blue|white|yellow|cyan|
783	     magenta`. The order in which they appear on the panel tells
784	     us unambiguously which byte order HEO actually wants.

792	  after every `gfxcCanvasUpdate(ISC_CANVAS_ID)`, so our

1177	(ARGB_8888). The canvas / Legato side configures and writes

1179	handler stores the canvas color mode into

1183	`XLCDC_SetLayerWindowXYSize`, `XLCDC_SetLayerXStride`,
1184	`XLCDC_SetLayerEnable`). So the boot value persists.
1185

1187	- Legato writes RGBA_8888: byte0=A, byte1=B, byte2=G, byte3=R
1188	- OVR1 reads ARGB_8888: byte0=B, byte1=G, byte2=R, byte3=A

1818	- `CSI2DC VPCFGR = 0x00004024` (PA bit set, change confirmed
1819	  in hardware).
1820	- `ISC_PFE_CFG0 = 0x50004080` (BPS=FORTY from D7 still in
1821	  effect).
1822	- `ISC_INTSR = 0x08000002 [HD HDTO ]` (HDTO still set).
1823	- `APP: heofb snap` pixels: `0xFF0070C1, 0xFF0050C1, ...,
1824	  0xFF005001, 0xFF003041, 0xFF004041, ...`
1825	    - byte 0 (B): `XX 000001` — bottom 6 bits ALWAYS
1826	      `000001`, top 2 bits varying.
1827	    - byte 1 (G): `XXXX 0000` — bottom 4 bits ALWAYS zero,
1828	      top 4 bits varying.
1829	    - byte 2 (R): always `0x00`.
1830	    - byte 3 (A): always `0xFF` (our alpha override).
1831	- User-visible: still "blue and green on top with flickering
1832	  color bars at bottom"; user asks "shouldn't source take
1833	  up full height of screen?"
1834	
1835	**Two important things this tells us:**
1836	
1837	1. The PA flip had **zero effect** on the framebuffer bit
1838	   pattern. The exact same nibble-stuck signature is present
1839	   with PA=0 (D7 era) and PA=1 (D8 era). My D8 root-cause
1840	   hypothesis is therefore **wrong**, and PA was never the
1841	   cause of the missing red channel. (PA=true is kept because
1842	   it matches the upstream Linux convention — see "Source
1843	   of truth" below.)
1844	2. The HEO geometry is correctly set up for full panel
1845	   height. `cfg2=0x00000028 (xpos=40,ypos=0)` and
1846	   `cfg3=0x01DF02CF (xsize=720,ysize=480)` describe a
1847	   720x480 region pillarboxed left/right inside the 800x480
1848	   panel — *the source is supposed to fill the whole vertical
1849	   extent*. The "top half good / bottom half bad" symptom
1850	   the user sees is therefore not a HEO-size problem; it's
1851	   that *the bottom half of the framebuffer in SDRAM*
1852	   contains different content than the top half.
1853	
1854	**Source of truth — Linux atmel-isc and atmel-csi2dc drivers**
1855	
1856	The Microchip-authored Linux kernel drivers for this exact
1857	silicon family (SAMA7G5 = SAM9X75 ISC IP block) are the
1858	authoritative reference for what the ISC pipeline can and
1859	cannot ingest. Two key tables:
1860	
1861	- `drivers/media/platform/microchip/microchip-sama7g5-isc.c`,
1862	  `sama7g5_formats_list[]` — the input formats the ISC's
1863	  PFE/RLP path supports:
1864	    - Bayer 8-bit (SBGGR8/SGBRG8/SGRBG8/SRGGB8): `BPS_EIGHT`
1865	    - Bayer 10-bit (SBGGR10/...): `BPS_TEN`
1866	    - Bayer 12-bit (SBGGR12/...): `BPS_TWELVE`
1867	    - GREY (Y8): `BPS_EIGHT`
1868	    - YUYV (YUV422 8-bit): `BPS_EIGHT` — 2 bytes/pixel
1869	    - UYVY (YUV422 8-bit): `BPS_EIGHT` — 2 bytes/pixel
1870	    - RGB565 (`RGB565_2X8_LE`): `BPS_EIGHT` — 2 bytes/pixel
1871	    - Y10: `BPS_TEN`
1872	- `drivers/media/platform/microchip/microchip-csi2dc.c`,
1873	  `csi2dc_formats[]` — the data types the CSI2DC supports:
1874	    - `RAW8` (DT=0x2A)
1875	    - `RAW10` (DT=0x2B)
1876	    - `YUV422_8B` (DT=0x1E)
1877	
1878	**Two structural facts fall out of these tables:**
1879	
1880	1. **`BPS_FORTY` is never used by Linux** for any MIPI input
1881	   format. Every supported MIPI format (YUV422, RGB565,
1882	   Bayer8, GREY) uses `BPS_EIGHT` for the per-component
1883	   width. The SAM9X75 manual's "FORTY: 40-bit input (used
1884	   for MIPI formats up to forty bits per pixel)" is a
1885	   residual encoding that the upstream driver never selects,
1886	   because none of the actually-supported MIPI input
1887	   formats need it. So the D7 hypothesis ("BPS must be
1888	   FORTY for any MIPI source") was **wrong**.
1889	2. **There is no entry for `RGB888` (3 bytes/pixel) anywhere**
1890	   — neither in `sama7g5_formats_list[]` nor in
1891	   `csi2dc_formats[]`. Linux does not support packed RGB888
1892	   over MIPI on this hardware. Our pipeline is currently
1893	   using `CSI_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888` and DT=0x24, which is
1894	   **outside the supported set**.
1895	
1896	The CSI2DC driver also tells us how PA is supposed to be
1897	programmed for serial sources (`csi2dc_vp_update()`):
1898	
1899	```c
1900	/* serial video pipeline */
1901	vp = CSI2DC_VPCFG_DT(...) ...;
1902	vp |= CSI2DC_VPCFG_VC(...) ...;
1903	vp &= ~CSI2DC_VPCFG_DE;
1904	vp |= CSI2DC_VPCFG_DM(CSI2DC_VPCFG_DM_DECODER8TO12);
1905	vp &= ~CSI2DC_VPCFG_DP2;
1906	vp &= ~CSI2DC_VPCFG_RMS;
1907	vp |= CSI2DC_VPCFG_PA;       // <-- always PA=1 for serial
1908	```
1909	
1910	So D8's PA=true is correct in principle — it matches the
1911	Linux convention exactly — it just was not the root cause
1912	of the channel-loss symptom we are chasing.
1913	
1914	**Why no `BPS` / `PA` / `RLP MODE` choice can make RGB888 work**
1915	
1916	The PFE / RLP pipeline in the SAM9X75 ISC is built around
1917	a model where each MIPI byte stream beat is *one ISC sample*.
1918	The downstream RLP modes assume a fixed number of beats per
1919	output pixel:
1920	
1921	- ARGB32 (`MODE = 0xA`) expects 24 bits of RGB packed in 3
1922	  consecutive 8-bit beats inside a single sample-slot
1923	  cadence — i.e. it expects the upstream to have already
1924	  grouped 3 bytes per pixel. With a 1-beat-per-sample MIPI
1925	  bus there's no architectural way to do that grouping
1926	  without a per-pixel state machine that doesn't exist in
1927	  the PFE. (This is why Linux pairs ARGB32 with parallel
1928	  Bayer + CFA + CC + CSC, where the byte-grouping happens
1929	  in CFA, **not** in the PFE.)
1930	- BYPASS (`MODE = 0xF`) is documented for "MIPI RMS" mode,
1931	  which requires `CSI2DC_VPCFGR.RMS = 1` — and `RMS` is
1932	  always cleared by the Linux CSI2DC driver, suggesting
1933	  RMS+BYPASS is for raw memory dumping, not display
1934	  pipelines.
1935	- The 16bpp MIPI modes (RGB565, YUV422) work because they
1936	  have a 2-byte-per-pixel cadence the PFE can sample
1937	  cleanly and the corresponding RLP modes (RGB565,
1938	  YYCC/YCYC) know how to repack them.
1939	
1940	There is no 24bpp / 3-byte-per-pixel ingest mode. The
1941	"stuck nibble" pattern we observe is the PFE doing
1942	*something* with the RGB888 byte stream — sampling it as
1943	if it were a wider format with embedded padding — and the
1944	RLP grabbing the wrong bits. No host-side knob fixes this
1945	because the issue is the absent format mapping, not a
1946	mis-set bit.
1947	
1948	**Fix direction (deferred, larger than a single edit)**
1949	
1950	The bridge — not the host — has to change. Two practical
1951	options:
1952	
1953	**Option A: TC358743 -> YUV422 (DT=0x1E, 2 bytes/pixel)**
1954	
1955	- Bridge: program `VOUT_SET2.SEL422 = 1` to enable YUV422
1956	  output, plus the bridge's CSC matrix to convert internal
1957	  RGB to BT.601 / BT.709 YCbCr. The TC358743 has hardware
1958	  CSC; previous attempts at "VOUT MANUAL" were partial
1959	  (CSC enable + matrix were missing). This time we'd need
1960	  the full CSC programming, not just the format bit.
1961	- Host CSI2DC: change `CSI2DC_VIDEO_PIPE_FORMAT_TYPE` from
1962	  `CSI2DC_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888` to a YUV422 equivalent (DT
1963	  0x1E). Verify the CSI2DC driver in this codebase
1964	  actually has a YUV422 format type, or add one.
1965	- Host ISC: `ISC_RLP_CFG.MODE = YYCC (0xB)` or
1966	  `YCYC (0xD)` (depending on bridge byte order); enable
1967	  ISC CSC (`ISC_CSC_Enable(1)`) for YCbCr -> RGB; possibly
1968	  enable Sub422 / Sub420 if needed for chroma upsampling.
1969	- Host DMA layout: probably stay at PACKED32 (RGB888 +
1970	  alpha) because the ISC CSC can write RGB out, even from
1971	  a YUV422 input — same HEO RGBMODE = 32bpp_ARGB8888
1972	  works.
1973	- Host framebuffer size: unchanged (W * H * 4) since DMA
1974	  output is still ARGB32 after ISC CSC.
1975	
1976	This is the "right" path that matches Linux's
1977	`MEDIA_BUS_FMT_YUYV8_2X8` exactly, and YUV422 over HDMI
1978	is a first-class format on consumer sources (many HDMI
1979	sinks negotiate it). The cost is the bridge-side CSC
1980	programming.
1981	
1982	**Option B: TC358743 -> RGB565 (DT=0x22, 2 bytes/pixel)**
1983	
1984	- Bridge: program output for RGB565 16bpp packed. The
1985	  TC358743 supports this; CSC is bridge-internal.
1986	- Host CSI2DC: DT=0x22 (RGB565 in CSI-2 spec).
1987	- Host ISC: `ISC_RLP_CFG.MODE = RGB565 (0x9)`,
1988	  `ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED16` (or whatever 16bpp layout exists),
1989	  no CSC needed.
1990	- Host framebuffer size: W * H * 2 (half what we have
1991	  now). HEO RGBMODE = 16bpp_RGB565.
1992	- Loses some colour fidelity (5/6/5 bits vs 8/8/8), but
1993	  no YUV/RGB conversion involved — simpler than YUV422.
1994	
1995	**Both options need a coordinated change to:**
1996	- `configuration.h` (CSI/CSI2DC/ISC format defines, RLP
1997	  mode, layout, framebuffer size).
1998	- TC358743 driver (bridge VOUT setup, CSC if YUV422).
1999	- App framebuffer allocation (`app.c` / `gfx_canvas_config.c`
2000	  if pixel size changes).
2001	- HEO layer programming
2002	  (`APP_ConfigureHEOForCameraFramebuffer()` RGBMODE).
2003	
2004	**Open question for the user:** which of A/B to pursue,
2005	or whether to first improve the diagnostic (cache-aware
2006	multi-row `heofb snap`) to pin down the bottom-half issue
2007	before pivoting to the format change.
2008	
2009	**Changes applied this cycle (purely housekeeping / no
2010	behavioural fix yet)**
2011	
2012	- `firmware/.../src/config/default/vision/drivers/isc/drv_isc.c`:
2013	  reverted D7's `if (enableMIPI) BPS_FORTY else ...`
2014	  branch. Restored the original `(4 - inputBits)` mapping
2015	  with a long block comment summarising D7's failure mode,
2016	  why Linux's per-component approach is correct, and why
2017	  the IMX219 path needs `BPS_TEN` (not `BPS_FORTY`).
2018	- `firmware/.../src/config/default/vision/image_sensors/tc358743/tc358743.c`:
2019	  rewrote the `tc358743_get_config()` block comment that
2020	  was claiming "BPS=FORTY for MIPI". Now points at this
2021	  cycle and explains the structural blocker.
2022	- `firmware/.../src/config/default/configuration.h`:
2023	  - `CSI2DC_POST_ALIGNED` kept at `true`. Comment rewritten
2024	    to attribute the choice to the Linux atmel-csi2dc

2028	    with the YUV422 / RGB565 follow-up plan so the next

2031	
2032	**Expected outcomes after flash (no behavioural change)**

2035	  back to `0b100 = EIGHT`), down from the D7 `0x50004080`
2036	  (BPS field `0b101 = FORTY`).
2037	- `CSI2DC VPCFGR` stays at **`0x00004024`** (PA=1 retained).

2046	- The user-visible change is therefore minor: the colour will

2053	
2054	## 5f. Cycle D10 — Pivot to YUV422 8-bit (UYVY) — minimal first pass
2055	
2056	**Premise**
2057	
2058	D9 established that the SAM9X75 ISC pipeline cannot ingest packed
2059	RGB888 over MIPI: the `(PFE -> RLP)` path has no 24bpp / 3-byte-per-
2060	pixel mode and there is no host-side knob to recover the missing
2061	red channel. Linux only supports 1- or 2-byte-per-pixel MIPI inputs
2062	on this hardware (Bayer 8/10/12, GREY, YUYV/UYVY, RGB565, Y10).
2063	
2064	D9 left two bridge options on the table:
2065	- **Option A:** TC358743 -> RGB565 (DT=0x22). User initially asked
2066	  for this.
2067	- **Option B:** TC358743 -> YUV422 8-bit / UYVY (DT=0x1E).
2068	
2069	Direct review of the upstream Linux driver
2070	(`drivers/media/i2c/tc358743.c`, `tc358743_g_mbus_config()` /
2071	`tc358743_set_csi_color_space()`) and the matching
2072	`tc358743_regs.h` shows that **the TC358743 only enumerates two
2073	CSI-2 output formats**:
2074	- `MEDIA_BUS_FMT_RGB888_1X24` (DT=0x24) — what we already had,
2075	  unsupported by the ISC.
2076	- `MEDIA_BUS_FMT_UYVY8_1X16` (DT=0x1E) — UYVY 4:2:2 8-bit.
2077	
2078	**RGB565 (DT=0x22) is not advertised by the bridge** in any
2079	combination of `VOUT_SET2` / `CONFCTL` settings the upstream
2080	driver knows about. The bridge has internal RGB565 *paths* but
2081	they are wired to the DPI/parallel output, not to the CSI-Tx PHY.
2082	
2083	That removes Option A as a viable path, and forces Option B. The
2084	user agreed (chat: *"Lets do option b"*).
2085	
2086	**Plan: minimal pass first ("option B-min")**
2087	
2088	Option B has two layers of complexity:
2089	1. Reconfigure the bridge + CSI2DC + ISC to actually move
2090	   YUV422 8-bit bytes into SDRAM in a `Y0/Cb/Y1/Cr` packed
2091	   layout.
2092	2. Make HEO display those bytes as colour-correct video
2093	   (either via HEO's native YCbCr mode + CSC matrix, or a
2094	   software YCbCr->RGB pass).
2095	
2096	D10 only does **(1)**. (2) is deferred to D11. The reasoning:
2097	- (1) is the structural change, and the framebuffer dump
2098	  (`APP: heofb snap`) already lets us validate it independently
2099	  of HEO — we just need to read the bytes in `Y0/Cb/Y1/Cr` order
2100	  instead of `A/R/G/B` order.
2101	- (2) requires programming HEO's `YCCEN` + `YCCMODE` bits,
2102	  picking BT.601 vs BT.709 vs full-range CSC matrix coefficients
2103	  for `LCDC_HEOCFG14..17`, and confirming HEO's chroma upsampling
2104	  for 4:2:2 -> 4:4:4 inside the layer. That's a separate piece
2105	  of code review and a separate failure mode to debug.
2106	- A small intermediate step is also required: HEO's RGBMODE
2107	  must be a **16bpp** format, otherwise its scan-line stride
2108	  would be twice the actual SDRAM stride, causing it to
2109	  over-fetch and tear into the next ring slot. We pick
2110	  `RGB565` (16bpp, RGBMODE=3) as the intermediate; this makes
2111	  HEO geometry/stride correct *but colours will be wrong* (HEO
2112	  will read each `Y0/Cb` byte pair as if it were a packed
2113	  RGB565 pixel — green-dominant noise garbled across the picture).
2114	  That mis-colour is the **expected** intermediate state; it's
2115	  the green-light that says "ISC bytes are in memory and HEO
2116	  is scanning them, all that's left is HEO interpreting them".
2117	
2118	**Bridge: TC358743 UYVY8_1X16 register sequence (mirrors Linux)**
2119	
2120	From `tc358743.c` `tc358743_set_csi_color_space()` and
2121	`tc358743_init_color_format_conversion()`:
2122	
2123	| Register | UYVY 8-bit value | Bits set / cleared |
2124	|----------|-----------------:|--------------------|
2125	| `VOUT_SET2`  (`0x8573`) | `0xC1` | `SEL422 \| VOUT_422FIL_100 \| COLORMODE_AUTO` |
2126	| `VI_REP`     (`0x8576`) | `0x60` | `VOUT_COLOR_601_YCBCR_LIMITED` (`0b011 << 5`) |
2127	| `CONFCTL`    (`0x0004`) | `0x0CD7` | `YCBCRFMT_422_8` set in field `[5:4]`; preserves rest of CONFCTL bits including `VBUFEN \| ABUFEN \| AUTOINDEX \| AUDOUTSEL \| AUDCHNUM_2` already set by D2/D3/D4 |
2128	| `VI_MODE`    (`0x8570`) | `0xE6` | `RGB_DVI = 0` (input is treated as TMDS HDMI; bridge applies its own RGB->YCbCr CSC) |
2129	
2130	`VOUT_SET2 = 0xC1` decodes as `SEL422=1 (YUV422 enabled)`,
2131	`VOUT_422FIL=2 (filter mode 100)`, `COLORMODE=AUTO (1)`. The AUTO
2132	colour mode lets the bridge derive the BT.601-vs-BT.709 matrix
2133	from input metadata; we set `VI_REP = LIMITED 601` so the YCbCr
2134	output is in the standard limited range that downstream HEO CSC
2135	will (eventually) decode without an extra scale step.
2136	
2137	These register writes also happen in the HDMIRST recovery path
2138	(`tc358743_pulse_csi_reset()`), which now restores the same
2139	`VOUT_SET2 / VI_REP / CONFCTL` set after pulsing HDMIRST so we
2140	don't silently fall back to the boot RGB888 setup mid-run.
2141	
2142	**CSI2DC, ISC, and configuration.h**
2143	
2144	| Macro | Old (D9) | New (D10) |
2145	|-------|----------|-----------|
2146	| `ISC_INPUT_FORMAT_TYPE`           | `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RGB`            | `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_YUV_422`        |
2147	| `ISC_INPUT_BIT_WIDTH`             | `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT`          | `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_8_BIT`          |
2148	| `ISC_OUTPUT_FORMAT_TYPE`          | `ISC_RLP_CFG_MODE_ARGB32 (0xA)`   | `ISC_RLP_CFG_MODE_YCYC (0xD)`     |
2149	| `ISC_OUTPUT_LAYOUT_TYPE`          | `ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED32`             | `ISC_LAYOUT_PACKED16`             |
2150	| `CSI_DATA_FORMAT_TYPE`            | `CSI2_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888`         | `CSI2_DATA_FORMAT_YUV422_8`       |
2151	| `CSI2DC_VIDEO_PIPE_FORMAT_TYPE`   | `CSI2DC_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888`       | `CSI2DC_DATA_FORMAT_YUV422_8`     |
2152	| `CSI2DC_DATA_PIPE_FORMAT_TYPE`    | `CSI2DC_DATA_FORMAT_RGB888`       | `CSI2DC_DATA_FORMAT_YUV422_8`     |
2153	| `CSI2DC_POST_ALIGNED`             | `true`                            | `true` (unchanged; matches Linux unconditional serial PA=1) |
2154	
2155	Per-frame buffer size therefore drops from `720*480*4 = 1.32 MiB`
2156	to `720*480*2 = 691 KiB`. `GBuffer` (`1920*1080*4*N`) stays
2157	oversized and unchanged.
2158	
2159	**App-side change: HEO RGBMODE + framebuffer snapshot**
2160	
2161	- `APP_CAMERA_FB_COLOR_MODE` -> `GFX_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565`
2162	  (matches the GFX canvas to a 16bpp pixel pitch so the canvas
2163	  driver computes XSTRIDE in 2 B/px units instead of 4).
2164	- `APP_CAMERA_HEO_RGB_MODE`  -> `XLCDC_RGB_COLOR_MODE_RGB_565`
2165	  (so HEO advances exactly one source row per panel row; colours
2166	  will be wrong, geometry will be right).
2167	- `APP_DumpHEOFramebufferSnapshot()` rewritten to decode each
2168	  sample point as a `Y0 / Cb / Y1 / Cr` macropixel and print
2169	  `Y=YY,YY Cb=YY Cr=YY` instead of a packed `0xAARRGGBB`. That
2170	  gives us per-component visibility:
2171	    - Luma should vary across the row with picture content.
2172	    - Cb / Cr should sit near `0x80` for desaturated content
2173	      and swing for saturated content.
2174	    - All-zero rows still flag the HDTO frame-truncation
2175	      regime that has been visible since D2.
2176	
2177	**Expected outcomes after flash**
2178	
2179	Pipeline registers:
2180	- `TC358743 VOUT_SET2 = 0xC1` (was `0x01`).
2181	- `TC358743 VI_REP = 0x60` (was `0x00`).
2182	- `TC358743 CONFCTL = 0x0CD7` post-start (was `0x0C17`).
2183	- `TC358743 VI_MODE = 0xE6` (unchanged; input still TMDS-HDMI).
2184	- `CSI : ... dataType=0x1E ...` (was `0x24`).
2185	- `CSI2DC VPdt=0x1E, DPdt=0x1E` (was `0x24`).
2186	- `CSI2DC VPCFGR = 0x0000401E` (DT field flipped to YUV422_8;
2187	  PA bit still set in `0x4000`).
2188	- `ISC_PFE_CFG0 = 0x40004080` (BPS still `EIGHT` per Linux for
2189	  any 8-bit-per-component MIPI format — D7 revert from D9
2190	  remains in effect).
2191	- `ISC_RLP_CFG = 0x0000FF0D` (MODE = `YCYC = 0xD`, alpha pad
2192	  byte = `0xFF` from D2 RLP fix; the alpha byte is unused by
2193	  the YCYC layout but the field is still written by the
2194	  driver).
2195	- `XLCDC HEO cfg1.RGBMODE = 3 (16bpp_RGB565)` (was `12`).
2196	
2197	User-visible:
2198	- Picture is **expected to be wrong colour** — most likely a
2199	  noisy green-dominant image with diagonal / vertical patterns
2200	  where the source has detail. That's HEO consuming
2201	  `Y0/Cb/Y1/Cr` byte pairs as RGB565 bits (Y0 lights up red+green
2202	  bits, Cb lights up blue bits in unpredictable combinations).
2203	  Important: the picture should now be **moving** with the
2204	  source content (luma variation), and should be **edge-to-
2205	  edge** vertically (no more bottom-half-zero, *if* we've

2208	- `APP: heofb snap` will print Y/Cb/Cr decoded values:
2209	    - `Y=XX,YY Cb=ZZ Cr=WW` — these are the bytes the panel
2210	      will eventually display correctly once D11 turns on
2211	      HEO YCCEN.
2212

7246	## 5t. Reference: CSI2DC <-> ISC handshake (PA + RMS interaction)
7247	
7248	**Purpose.** A permanent reference for what the two SAM9X75
7249	`CSI2DC_VPCFGR` host-side knobs (`PA` bit 14, `RMS` bit 13) actually
7250	do to the byte stream the ISC sees. Future agents who flip either
7251	bit should re-read this section first — both bits jointly define
7252	the *contract* between CSI2DC and the ISC PFE/RLP, and they are
7253	easy to confuse.
7254	
7255	### What each bit really controls
7256	
7257	`PA` (Post Adjustment, bit 14) — *byte alignment within an ISC slot.*
7258	
7259	- `PA=0`: video-pipe output bytes are **LSB-aligned** in each 12-bit
7260	  ISC sample slot. An 8-bit byte `0xB4` lands as bits[7:0] = `0xB4`,
7261	  bits[11:8] = `0x0`.
7262	- `PA=1`: bytes are **MSB-aligned**. An 8-bit byte `0xB4` lands as
7263	  bits[11:4] = `0xB4`, bits[3:0] = `0x0`.
7264	
7265	PA matters when the ISC PFE samples something other than the full
7266	12-bit slot: BPS=EIGHT samples the lower 8 bits, BPS=TWELVE samples
7267	all 12. With `PA=1 + BPS=EIGHT`, the PFE reads bits[7:0] which are
7268	the four LSBs of the source byte plus four padding zeros — i.e.
7269	`(src_byte & 0x0F) << 4`. With `PA=0 + BPS=EIGHT`, the PFE reads
7270	the source byte intact.
7271	
7272	`RMS` (Recommended Memory Storage, bit 13) — *output pacing model.*
7273	
7274	- `RMS=0`: video-pipe outputs **1 pixel per component per ISPCK
7275	  clock**, formatted for the ISC processing engine's expected
7276	  per-component cadence. For a YUV422 source, that means alternating
7277	  Cb/Y/Cr/Y components paced one-per-clock, each in its own 12-bit
7278	  slot (with PA controlling alignment within the slot).
7279	- `RMS=1`: video-pipe generates a **raw byte stream compliant with
7280	  the CSI-2 specification memory format**, one byte per ISPCK clock,
7281	  no per-component slotting.
7282	
7283	RMS therefore changes the *upstream byte rate* (RMS=1 is roughly 1
7284	byte per clock, RMS=0 is 1 component per clock = 1 byte per clock
7285	for 8-bit YUV422 too — but the framing of those bytes differs).
7286	
7287	### The pre-D27 misconfiguration
7288	
7289	Before D27 the host was running `PA=1 + RMS=0 + RLP MODE=DAT8`.
7290	That combination is internally inconsistent:
7291	
7292	- `PA=1 + RMS=0` says "format the input for the ISC processing
7293	  engine, MSB-aligned in 12-bit slots." The ISC processing engine
7294	  here means YYCC/YCYC/RGB-style RLP modes that are aware of
7295	  per-component slot semantics.
7296	- `RLP MODE=DAT8` says "raw 8-bit pass-through." This is Linux's
7297	  `V4L2_PIX_FMT_GREY` mapping — it expects a flat byte stream, not
7298	  per-component-paced 12-bit slots.
7299	
7300	The resulting symptom in the 2026-04-28 D26 boot log against real
7301	SMPTE 75 % bars: every captured byte was in the `0x08..0x37` range,
7302	i.e. far below the `0x10..0xB4` luma span of real bars. That is
7303	plausibly explained by the RLP DAT8 picking up a slice of the
7304	12-bit slot (e.g. bits[7:0] under PA=1) rather than the source
7305	byte itself, attenuating each value by roughly a factor of 16 or
7306	producing a nibble-shifted value.
7307	
7308	### Consistent host-side pairings (treat as the menu of options)
7309	
7310	| RLP MODE | Recommended PA | Recommended RMS | Notes |
7311	|---|---|---|---|
7312	| `DAT8` (raw byte pass-through, Linux GREY) | `0` (LSB) or `1` with care | `1` (byte stream) | Use byte-stream pacing; PA can be either since the RLP only takes raw bytes anyway. **D27 chooses PA=1 + RMS=1** to keep PA at the Linux baseline. |
7313	| `YYCC` / `YCYC` / `YYRR`-style YUV packers | `1` (Linux upstream) | `0` (per-component) | These RLP modes are 12-bit-slot-aware. Use Linux's PA=1 + RMS=0 baseline. |
7314	| `ARGB32` / RGB packers | `1` (Linux upstream) | `0` (per-component) | Same as YUV packer rationale. |
7315	
7316	When the RLP MODE is changed in a future cycle, **revisit PA + RMS
7317	together** and check this table.
7318	
7319	### Diagnostic value: which knob to reach for first
7320	
7321	If captured bytes look smoothly varying but heavily attenuated or
7322	nibble-shifted (typical fingerprint: amplitude crammed into a
7323	`~0x08..0x40` band with all values having low-LSB-only entropy) and
7324	the RLP is in a raw mode (`DAT8` / `DATY8`), suspect the PA + RMS
7325	contract first. Cheaper than auditing PFE BPS or sync-polarity bits.
7326	
7327	If captured bytes have full dynamic range but the wrong byte
7328	positions are populated (e.g. `XX 00 00 00` cadence), suspect the
7329	RLP packer mode itself or its `YMODE` sub-field, not PA / RMS.

7344	Source: 720x480p60 RGB on the HDMI cable; bridge config
7345	`VOUT_SET2=0xC1`, `CONFCTL.YCBCRFMT=3`, `VI_REP=0x60` (UYVY 4:2:2

7350	| TC358743 video output | UYVY 4:2:2 8-bit, DT=0x1E | 720 px × 2 B = **1440 B** | 480 lines × 1440 B = **691,200 B** |

7354	| ISC RLP | `MODE=DAT8` (1 B per PFE sample) | 1440 B | matches PFE expectation |
7355	| ISC DMA descriptor | `DCFG.IMODE=PACKED8`, slot=`FRAME_BUFFER_SIZE(720,480,8)` | 720 B per DMA "row" | **345,600 B per slot** (= 720 × 480) |
7356	| DMA ring | `descCount=2`, slots at `0x21000000` and `0x21054600` | — | **691,200 B total** |

7358	### Two coupled framing bugs
7359	
7360	**Bug A — PFE row-axis is doubled.**
7361	`PFE_CFG2.ROWMAX = 959 = 2*vpix - 1`. The firmware comment in
7362	`drv_isc.c` (around line 810) and §5m / D17 both flagged this `*2`
7363	on rows as suspicious-but-copied-from-Linux, and §5m claimed it was
7364	"harmless because ROWMAX higher than the actual frame height just
7365	upper-bounds the row counter." The D27 boot log contradicts that:
7366	
7367	- `isc{isr=248 vd=248 ddone=0 ...}` — VD fires every source VSYNC
7368	  (≈4 s of real time), but DMA descriptor-done has **never** fired
7369	  since stream start. Exactly what you'd expect if the PFE row
7370	  counter never reaches ROWMAX → ISC never asserts the per-frame
7371	  end-of-frame signal that the DMA controller uses to advance to
7372	  the next descriptor.
7373	- Steady-state `peek=0x08000002` (HD + HDTO) is consistent with
7374	  PFE blocking, waiting for a row-counter event that never comes.

7377	`vpix << 1`.
7378	
7379	**Bug B — DMA slot is half a source frame.**

7381	RLP=DAT8 and PFE COLMAX=1439, every source MIPI line writes
7382	**1440 contiguous bytes** into the ring, so:

7384	- One source frame = 691,200 B = exactly **two slots**.
7385	- One source MIPI line = **two** PACKED8 "rows" of 720 B in the

7402	`APP_DumpHEOFramebufferSnapshot()` computes window addresses with
7403	`bytesPerRow = imageWidth = 720`, i.e. it assumes one DMA row =

7405	factor of two on the row axis**: each DMA row is half of a source
7406	MIPI line. Concretely:

7409	  `N/2`, byte `0..31` (= source pixels `0..15` of that line).

## 2. Pipeline mental model they settled on

Key findings in §5t and §5u:

- **PA** (VPCFGR bit 14): byte alignment within the 12-bit ISC slot. `PA=1` = MSB-aligned (Linux convention for all serial modes).
- **RMS** (VPCFGR bit 13): upstream pacing. `RMS=0` = one *component* per ISPCK clock (per-component framing expected by YYCC/YCYC/ARGB32 packers). `RMS=1` = raw CSI-2 byte stream, one byte per clock.
- **RLP MODE's role** (from §5e/D9): each RLP mode assumes a fixed number of upstream *beats per output pixel*. `BYPASS` samples 32 bits/cycle from PFE→RLP bus → with a 16-bit-wide MIPI datapath you get 16 real + 16 zero per cycle. `ARGB32` expects 3 RGB bytes pre-grouped in one slot cadence — **the PFE cannot do that grouping for MIPI**; Linux only uses ARGB32 when CFA (Bayer) does the grouping upstream.
- **ISC counts samples (slot cadence), not pixels.** Under BPS=EIGHT the PFE samples one 8-bit component per cycle; under PACKED32 the DMA emits one 32-bit memory word per RLP cycle → live byte at b0, three zero-padding bytes at b1/b2/b3. **This is their explanation for your exact `[XX 00 00 00]` symptom.**
- **Consistent pairings table (treat as menu):** DAT8 → PA=1 + RMS=1. YYCC/YCYC/ARGB32 → PA=1 + RMS=0.

## 3. Full-frame written to memory?

**Yes — first at D35** (`YYCC + RMS=0 + PA=1 + PACKED32`): data through y=479, DMA fills full allocated slot, cliff gone. Before D35, every cycle had a cliff — most often at source row ~168 (D21–D34), or at ~80 MIPI lines (D27) or ~160 (D11). The cliff at **~168** was independent of bandwidth (D34 proved it by disabling HEO). The cliff broke when RMS flipped 1→0 **and** RLP went from BYPASS→YYCC in the same cycle.

## 4. Correctly-decoded byte content?

**D36** produced dense `Cb Y0 Cr Y1` UYVY macropixels — first time red ever appeared on panel. User confirmed by visual (no byte-level validation against SMPTE bar values was ever completed — deferred).

## 5. Dead ends — do not re-walk

1. **RGB888 DT=0x24 is structurally unsupported.** No combination of BPS/PA/RMS/RLP MODE makes it work. Linux's `sama7g5_formats_list[]` has no 24bpp/3-byte-per-pixel entry; neither does `csi2dc_formats[]`. **This is the single most important finding for you.** Your current pipeline is RGB888+ARGB32, and your `[only b0 live]` symptom is the identical fingerprint.
2. **BPS=FORTY for MIPI (D7)**: Linux never uses FORTY for any MIPI format; every Linux MIPI path uses BPS=EIGHT. Don't try FORTY.
3. **PA alone** does not recover missing channels (D8 ruled out).
4. **AHB/DDR2 bandwidth** is not the cause of cliffs (D34 ruled out by disabling HEO; HDTO still fires at same row).
5. **BEATS16/BEATS32**: D14 showed BEATS32 too aggressive; D32 showed BEATS16 no improvement; IMX219 baseline runs BEATS8 — stick with BEATS8.
6. **PFE crop (COLEN/ROWEN + COLMAX/ROWMAX) from D17** is innocent; D33 reverted it with no effect on cliff.
7. **CSC/Sub422 pipeline stages** — Linux only enables them for RAW→YUV conversion; for already-YUV or already-RGB sources, `bits_pipeline=0`. Don't enable them as a first experiment.
8. **CSI2DC GISR=0x10 is benign** (bit 4 = VP capture complete, NOT DED which is bit 7). Earlier cycles misidentified this.

## 6. Datasheet/register insights

- **`ISC_DCTRL.IE` has INVERTED polarity** on this IP block. DFP header: `IE_0_Val=0 → "DDONE interrupt is generated"`. Linux `microchip-isc-base.c:194` writes `ISC_DCTRL_IE_IS = (0x0 << 4)`. Every pre-D31 cycle had IE=1 which **suppresses DDONE**. This alone explains `ddone=0` forever. **Check your `ISC_DCTRL` reads 0x00000001, not 0x00000011.**
- `PFE_CFG2.ROWMAX = 2*vpix - 1` pattern copied from Linux was wrong-but-plausible (journal flagged as suspect pre-D28 but cleared it later).
- CSI2DC `VPCFG_DM = DECODER8TO12` is Linux's serial-mode constant.
- `bufferSize` must equal the **memory byte rate per source frame**, not `W*H*(IMODE_bpp/8)`. YYCC+PACKED8 on UYVY 4:2:2 source = `W*H*2` (16 bpp-equivalent), not `W*H*1`. D36's seam at row 240 was a slot=half-frame bug from this mistake.

Your current state (RGB888 DT=0x24 → ARGB32 RLP → PACKED32, symptom: only byte 0 of each 4-byte slot is live) is **exactly the D0-D9 failure fingerprint.** Per D9, the SAM9X75 ISC PFE/RLP **cannot ingest 24bpp packed RGB888 over MIPI** — there is no 3-byte-per-pixel sampling mode. The previous engineer pivoted the TC358743 to UYVY 4:2:2 (DT=0x1E) at D10 and never went back. If you stick with RGB888+ARGB32, D9's diagnosis says no host-side knob will make it work.

Two gotchas to check on your very first boot before doing anything else:
1. `ISC_DCTRL` must read `0x00000001` (IE=0). If it reads `0x00000011`, DDONE is suppressed — fix inverted-polarity `IE` first.
2. `bufferSize` must equal real memory byte rate per source frame (for RGB888 ARGB32 PACKED32 that's `720*480*4=1,382,400 B`; for your `only 181 of 480 rows written` symptom, also check whether slot size is half of what it should be — the D36 seam-at-240 signature).

You're right. Pulled the datasheet — **RGB888 is explicitly supported**, and I've been running the wrong RLP mode.

**ISC_RLP_CFG.MODE field (DS60001813D, page 1443–1445):**

| Value | Name | Description |
|---|---|---|
| 10 | ARGB32 | 24-bit RGB + 8-bit Alpha |
| 15 | **BYPASS** | **32-bit input is sampled and written to the rlp output port. Select this mode for MIPI RMS mode.** |

Two things jump out:

1. **ARGB32 (MODE=10) is literally defined as "24-bit RGB + 8-bit Alpha"** — it IS the RGB888 path. My current config (`rlpMode = ISC_RLP_CFG_MODE_ARGB32`) is the intended mode. The prior engineer's D0–D9 "RGB888 isn't supported" conclusion was an inference from driver-table policy (Linux's `sama7g5_formats_list[]` omits it), not from the hardware.

2. **BYPASS (MODE=15) is the explicit recommendation for MIPI+RMS mode.** Its description says so verbatim. For our CSI2DC-is-emitting-byte-stream-at-RMS=1 setup, BYPASS is the datasheet-sanctioned choice. The prior engineer stumbled onto BYPASS at D29 (with UYVY source, not RGB888) and got full-slot data — then moved on before closing the loop on why.

**Working theory revised:** Either MODE=10 (ARGB32) is the right mode but needs RMS=0 so upstream hands it pre-grouped pixels, OR MODE=15 (BYPASS) is right with our current RMS=1 and LAYOUT=PACKED32, and my current `[b0 live, b1/b2/b3 zero, 181 rows]` result is because I'm running MODE=10 while CSI2DC is in byte-stream mode — a mismatch the datasheet specifically warns about.

## Before we act, let me verify two more datasheet points

- The CSI2DC RGB888 memory-format description I found earlier shows `{B2,R1,G1,B1}` then `{G3,B3,R2,G2}` packed into 32-bit words — that's the byte-stream layout that RMS=1 + BYPASS should preserve end-to-end. I want to read the CSI2DC VP chapter alongside the ISC RLP/PFE chapter to confirm how they handshake.
- Also want to confirm PFE CFG0 MIPI=1 interacts cleanly with RMS=1 upstream — the prior engineer hinted there may be a "pair these correctly" constraint that's explicit in the text.

Let me fetch those pages to have a complete picture before I propose a concrete config change.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 21:07:11Z)**_

Datasheet confirms the picture more precisely:

**IMODE → rlp_data bus (DS60001813D page 1353, Figure 50.44):**

The DMA just samples N bits off the 32-bit `rlp_data` bus per cycle and writes them:
- PACKED8 → `rlp_data[7:0]`
- PACKED16 → `rlp_data[15:0]`
- PACKED32 → `rlp_data[31:0]`

What drives `rlp_data` is the **RLP module**:
- **BYPASS (MODE=15):** "32-bit input is sampled and written to the rlp output port. **Select this mode for MIPI RMS mode.**" → `rlp_data[31:0]` = 32 bits straight from upstream per clock.
- **ARGB32 (MODE=10):** "24-bit RGB + 8-bit Alpha" → `rlp_data[31:0]` = `{ALPHA_REG, R, G, B}` — the pipeline must deliver 24 bits of RGB per pixel cycle.

**The mismatch explains my exact symptom.** My current state is **RLP=ARGB32 + IMODE=PACKED32 + CSI2DC RMS=1**:
- RMS=1 tells CSI2DC to emit a byte-stream (one byte per clock)
- ARGB32 expects per-pixel 24-bit RGB arriving on the pipeline per clock
- Result: RLP produces a partially-populated 32-bit word per input byte; only one lane lines up with valid data. That's exactly the `[b0 live, b1/b2/b3 zero]` I'm seeing. And the "181 of 480 rows" is the rate mismatch burning through the descriptor budget.

The journal's "local fix that added RMS=1 to plib_csi2dc.c" was the actual bug — it paired RMS=1 with the ARGB32 RLP mode that wants RMS=0. The 60fps was just "frames are flowing" without byte-level validation.

## Two datasheet-sanctioned paths for RGB888

| Option | RLP MODE | RMS | IMODE | `dma.size` | Memory layout |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **A** | **BYPASS (15)** | **1** (byte stream) | PACKED32 | `W×H×3` | Tightly packed `R0G0B0R1G1B1…` — 1⅓ pixels per 32-bit word |
| **B** | **ARGB32 (10)** | **0** (per-component per clock) | PACKED32 | `W×H×4` | `{A,R,G,B}` — one pixel per 32-bit word, display-ready |

**Option B is what we actually want** (Legato displays ARGB32 natively, no conversion pass), and it's the cleanest two-line change:
1. `plib_csi2dc.c`: drop the `| CSI2DC_VPCFGR_RMS_1` OR-in — set RMS=0 (matches Linux canonical).
2. `isc_capture.c`: already correct (RLP=ARGB32, PACKED32, BPP=4).

Plus a sanity check I'd like to add: print `ISC_DCTRL` at start so we can confirm IE polarity the prior engineer warned about.

Shall I make that change and you flash? Expect: 60 fps sustained, full 480 rows written, b1/b2/b3 now carrying R/G/B bytes. From there we verify source color decodes correctly.

Register dump looks clean: `ISC_DCTRL=0x00000001` (IE=0, DE=1, correct), `ISC_DCFG=0x00000022` (PACKED32 + BEATS8), `ISC_RLP_CFG=0x0000000A` (MODE=ARGB32), `CSI2DC_VPCFGR=0x00004024` (DT=0x24, PA=1, **RMS=0**).

**Conclusion:** ARGB32 RLP mode on this IP block does NOT reassemble a byte-stream into pixels — it needs the pipeline stages upstream (CFA/WB/Gamma/CSC) to deliver pre-grouped `{R,G,B}` per clock. With those bypassed for `DRV_IMAGE_SENSOR_RGB`, ARGB32 writes one sample per 32-bit slot and zero-pads the rest, regardless of RMS. The prior engineer's D9 diagnosis was correct for this specific angle.

That leaves the datasheet's explicit MIPI-RMS path: **BYPASS RLP (MODE=15) + RMS=1 + PACKED32**. The datasheet literally says "Select this mode for MIPI RMS mode." The prior engineer tried BYPASS on UYVY (D29) and got full-slot writes; they never tried BYPASS on RGB888.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 21:19:55Z)**_

**Huge step forward.** Registers are right (`RLP_CFG=0x0F`, `DCFG=0x20`, `VPCFGR=0x6024`), and we now have meaningful byte content. `90 C0 60 90` repeating at TM across all probes = a genuine solid-color region at pixel (360,0) of some actual color, with black edges at TL/TR — that's consistent with a real image (letterboxed content), not noise.

But the cliff is now at **row 60**, even worse than before. 60×720×3 = 129,600 bytes per frame = **exactly 1/8** of the 1,036,800-byte budget. The `8:1` ratio is suspicious and the prior journal's D27/D31/D34 showed RMS=1 consistently hit cliffs regardless of burst size or HEO — they concluded RMS=1 mode itself has a rate/backpressure problem the ISC can't drain. Only D35's RMS=0 cleared every cliff.

On the byte content: `R=0x60 G=0xC0 B=0x90` in BGR order = teal-cyan, not orange. Two possibilities: (a) the pipeline is doing an unwanted color transform, or (b) the source content at pixel (360,0) genuinely isn't the solid orange — could be a letterbox/title-bar region of the Wii's actual output. The TL/TR being `00 00 00` (black) at the same row is consistent with black side-bars. We can't resolve that until we have a full frame to inspect.

**Next move: try RMS=0 + DAT8 (MODE=0) + PACKED8.** This is the "cleanest" RMS=0 path — DAT8 literally means "8-bit data" per the datasheet, and RMS=0 lets CSI2DC throttle to ISC pipeline rate (which is what cleared the prior engineer's cliff at D35). Keeps PACKED8 and BPP=3, so memory layout stays the same as now.

Also adding VPCOLR/VPROWR to the probe dump so we can see what CSI2DC thinks the last-received column/row was — that directly tells us whether ISC is the bottleneck or upstream is cutting data.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 21:27:22Z)**_

**Breakthrough — VPROW=241 is the smoking gun.** Two decoupled issues, only one of them is the ISC pipeline:

## Issue 1 (upstream): CSI2DC only sees 241 rows per frame, not 480

`VPCOL=720 VPROW=241` means CSI2DC is receiving full-width lines, but only ~half the frame's worth of them. Every probe, every frame. The ISC isn't at fault — it's faithfully capturing what's delivered. 241 ≈ 480/2 strongly suggests **the source path is 480i (interlaced), not 480p**, even though TC358743 reports "p" in our detection code. 60 fps × 241 rows = 60 fields/sec of a 240-line field = classic 480i @ 60 Hz.

Worth checking: does the Wii output component as 480p natively, or is it 480i being upconverted by ElectronWarp? Or TC358743 is misreporting the "p" flag but passing through fields.

## Issue 2 (ISC side): 1 byte per pixel instead of 3

Recomputing iter 4 in light of VPROW=241: DMA wrote 173,520 bytes (= 241 × 720 × **1**, not × 3). My probe was interpreting that with a 2160-byte stride (`W×3`) and seeing it as "80 rows". Correct stride is 720 bytes. So iter 4 actually captured **every row CSI2DC delivered**, just at 1 byte per pixel — DAT8 + RMS=0 samples one 8-bit component per pixel clock, missing the other two.

This is actually significant diagnostic progress: **ISC can drain everything upstream delivers. There's no ISC cliff in RMS=0 mode** (ratio of bytes-written : bytes-delivered was 1/3 in iter 4, but that's exactly the bytes-per-pixel reduction, not a cliff).

## Novelty audit

- Iter 3 (BYPASS + PACKED8 + RMS=1): novel — real BGR triples, cliff confirmed RMS=1-induced.
- Iter 4 (DAT8 + PACKED8 + RMS=0): novel — no cliff, but 1-byte-per-pixel truncation.
- Prior engineer never tested these RGB888 combos, never used VPCOLR/VPROWR for diagnosis, never decoupled upstream rows from ISC bytes.

We're genuinely narrowing.

**ISC side: unambiguous diagnosis from iter 5.**

- `VPCOL=720 VPROW=241` identical to iter 4 — **the 241-row upstream limit is independent of ISC config**.
- 241 rows captured at 4 bytes/pixel = 694,080 bytes/frame, matching DMA output exactly. No cliff, no truncation.
- Byte content at TM: `C0 02 00 00` = 32-bit word `0x000002C0`. Only **one** of the four bytes has meaningful data (`0xC0`), three are zero.

The `0xC0` matches the **G** byte of the user's claimed source color `R=FF G=C0 B=80`. That's too clean to be coincidence: **CSI2DC in RMS=0 mode is NOT decomposing RGB888 per-component as it does for YUV422 — it's emitting one byte per pixel (probably the G component) and zeroing the rest.** This is likely why Linux's format table omits RGB888 for the VP's RMS=0 decoder path.

## Where we actually are

| Config | Cliff? | Data density | Content correctness |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Iter 3** (BYPASS + PACKED8 + RMS=1) | **Yes** — 60 rows captured of 241 delivered (~25%) | 3 bytes/pixel correct | Real BGR triples |
| **Iter 4** (DAT8 + PACKED8 + RMS=0) | No — 241/241 | 1 byte/pixel | Just one component (G?) |
| **Iter 5** (BYPASS + PACKED32 + RMS=0) | No — 241/241 | 4 bytes/pixel but 3 are zero | Same single-component problem as iter 4, padded |

**The decomposer chain — CSI2DC VP → ISC pipeline — doesn't have a working RGB888 path in RMS=0 because CSI2DC VP's RMS=0 output only emits one byte per pixel clock for DT=0x24, not three.** RMS=1 byte-stream delivery works, but the ISC has a ~1/4 throughput cliff on it (prior engineer's D27/D31/D34 hit the same class of cliff and never cracked it in 37 cycles).

So RGB888 is "supported" by hardware (the data types are defined, registers exist), but the combination "RGB888 + full-bandwidth RMS=1 ingest through VP→ISC" appears to be what's failing.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 21:39:54Z)**_

**Dense dump was exactly what we needed.** Four key findings:

1. **b2 and b3 are universally 0x00** across 48 bytes × 3 rows × 4 probes × hundreds of pixels. Not "usually zero" — **always** zero. Those byte lanes carry no data.
2. **b1 always uses only the low nibble (0x00–0x0F).** Upper nibble of b1 is zero everywhere.
3. Combining 1+2: each pixel word is effectively **12 bits of data** — b0 (upper 8 bits) + b1's low nibble (lower 4 bits). That's a 12-bit sample, MSB-aligned in the upper 8 bits — exactly what PA=1 + the 12-bit ISC bus would produce.
4. **b0 is locally uniform but varies by row:** row 0 ≈ 0xC0, row 30 ≈ 0xC0, row 100 ≈ 0x60. Within a row, 12 consecutive pixels have the same byte.

## Interpretation

Confirmed: **CSI2DC RMS=0 on DT=0x24 outputs one 12-bit sample per pixel clock**, not three 8-bit components. That 12-bit sample is the *full source pixel* only if the source IS 12-bit, but for a 24-bit RGB888 pixel arriving over MIPI, CSI2DC collapses to some component. Whatever that component happens to be, *we can't recover the other two*.

Now, 0xC0 at row 0 = G of the claimed orange. 0x60 at row 100 = R of something else. If the source were truly solid R=FF/G=C0/B=80 over the whole screen, row 0 and row 100 would read the same byte. They don't — so either **the source isn't uniformly colored end-to-end** (likely: Wii menu/game screens have top/mid/bottom content bands), or CSI2DC rotates which component it samples per row. Either way, Phase 5b's "identical solid color everywhere" assumption is weaker than we thought and we can't use it to decode byte layout definitively.

## Question for you before iter 3

**Is the Wii source actually uniform R=FF G=C0 B=80 across the entire 720×480 raster, or is that just the color of one region (the game area) with the rest being UI/border content?** The answer changes what we expect from iter 3.

**Important implication from uniform source:** in iter 5 we saw row 0 = `0xC0` (G byte of full-range R=FF/G=C0/B=80) and row 100 = `0x60` (no component match). If the source is genuinely uniform end-to-end, **different rows capturing different bytes is a capture-pipeline artifact, not source content.** That confirms my "CSI2DC RMS=0 on RGB888 captures one component per pixel with row-dependent phase" theory — the phase counter isn't resetting per row so different rows land on different component clocks (R→G→B cycle). Any single-component mode is useless for RGB888 regardless of which component it picks.

**Limited-range + A2D caveats noted** — I won't expect byte-exact matches to any of `FF/C0/80` or the limited-range `EB/B5/7E`. Bytes will drift ±few LSB and likely sit between full- and limited-range values depending on where in the pipeline the range conversion happens.

## What to watch for in iter 6 (BYPASS + PACKED8 + RMS=1 + BPP=3)

iter 6 is staged. With byte-stream capture of a uniform source, the dense dump should show a **clean 3-byte repeating pattern**:

```
r  0 x360+: XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ ...
r 10 x360+: XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ ...    (same values)
r 50 x360+: XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ XX YY ZZ ...    (same values if within cliff)
r100 x360+: 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 ...    (past cliff)
r200 x360+: 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 55 ...    (past cliff)
```

Where `XX/YY/ZZ` should be approximately `{B, G, R}` of the source — somewhere in the neighborhood of `7E/B5/EB` (limited) to `80/C0/FF` (full) with A2D drift.

The left-edge dump at `r0 x0+` will tell us whether there's genuinely no black margin, i.e., whether pixel (0,0) also has the uniform color or if it's actually black. If the source is truly uniform, pixel (0,0) should also read as real color bytes — which would mean my earlier probe showing `TL (0,0): 00 00 00 00` was misleading (perhaps ISC writes that region as zero for some startup reason).

If we see the expected 3-byte repeating pattern: **iter 3 config is the correct RGB888 capture path.** The only remaining ISC-side problem is then the RMS=1 cliff, and we can reason about that with real data.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 21:47:46Z)**_

**Major win: iter 6 captures real repeating RGB data.** Look at the dense dumps:

```
r  0 x  0+: ...00000000 00000060 90C06090 C06090C0 6090C060 90C06090 C06090C0
r  0 x360+: 90C06090 C06090C0 6090C060 90C06090 C06090C0 6090C000 00000000...
r 10 x360+: ...00000000 00000060 90C06090 C06090C0 6090C060 90C06090 C06090C0
```

That's a **perfect repeating `90 C0 60` 3-byte cycle** sitting in memory across multiple rows. This is genuine per-pixel RGB888 content, faithfully captured. The pipeline works.

## Reading the actual bytes

Pattern: `90 C0 60` in memory byte order. Three ways to interpret:

| Interpretation | R | G | B | vs your source (FF/C0/80) |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| BGR | 0x60 | 0xC0 | 0x90 | R mismatch big, B off by +16 |
| RGB | 0x90 | 0xC0 | 0x60 | R off by -111, B off by -32 |
| GRB | 0xC0 | 0x90 | 0x60 | G=R swap looks weird |

**G=0xC0 matches your source exactly no matter which interpretation we pick.** That's not random — the G component is almost certainly correct. R and B are both *lower* than expected, which is consistent with an A2D stage that has lower headroom (can't swing to 0xFF or even close). An A2D that clips/compresses bright R would leave G (middle value) intact and drag R and B down — that's a real, common analog-chain artifact.

## Two weird things in the memory layout

1. **~27-byte leading zeros per row before pattern starts** (r0 x0, r10 x360), and **pattern ends mid-row** (r0 x360 dies at byte ~1101). Looks like pattern covers roughly the middle ~350 pixels of the 720-pixel row, zeros on the edges.

2. **Phase shift:** at byte 27 the cycle starts `60 90 C0`, at byte 1080 it starts `90 C0 60`. Both offsets are multiples of 3 so phase "should" match if the layout were clean 3-byte-per-pixel — but it doesn't.

3. **`VPCOL=540`** (was 720 in RMS=0 iters). With RMS=1 this probably counts something like 4-byte-aligned bursts or a different metric. `540 × 4 = 2160 = full row data in bytes` — so VP is delivering the full row worth of bytes, just counted differently.

## Where we are

**Genuine capture works.** That's the big unlock. Remaining open items on the ISC side:

- **Cliff at 60 source rows** (still, same as iter 3).
- **Pattern only covers ~50% of each captured row** (zeros on edges) — possibly because CSI2DC starts/stops the byte stream with the active video region narrower than the 720-pixel raster the TC358743 reports. Could be a TC358743 active-area config issue, not ISC.
- **Phase misalignment between rows** — probably because leading/trailing zero counts per row aren't constant, so each row's pattern start drifts relative to the byte-0 alignment of the stride-2160 probe. That's a memory-layout consequence of issue above, not a separate bug.

Great plan — solid R, G, B is exactly the controlled-input test that'll disambiguate byte order and tell us if each channel has different A2D response. With the current iter 6 build already on the device, no reflash needed. Just change the source between captures.

**What I'll be looking for in each log:**

| Source | Expected pattern (if BGR) | Expected pattern (if RGB) |
|---|---|---|
| Solid R (full-range 255,0,0) | `00 00 XX` repeating (XX ≈ 0x90-ish given A2D droop) | `XX 00 00` |
| Solid G (0,255,0) | `00 XX 00` | `00 XX 00` (same either way) |
| Solid B (0,0,255) | `XX 00 00` | `00 00 XX` |

If **R** shows data in the third byte position (bytes 2/5/8/...) and **B** shows data in the first byte position (bytes 0/3/6/...), the order is **BGR**.

If the other way around, it's **RGB**.

G test is the sanity check — whichever way, it lands in the middle byte.

Also watch:
- **Whether each channel hits the same peak value.** If R peaks at `0x90` but G peaks at `0xC0` and B peaks at `0x60`, that's per-channel A2D gain asymmetry — useful to know and correctable in software later.
- **Whether the pattern coverage of the row changes with color.** The ~50% coverage with zeros on edges we saw earlier might be content-dependent or might be fixed regardless of color. If the pure-color tests show different coverage, interesting. If identical, it's a structural TC358743/pipeline issue independent of content.
- **Whether VPCOL/VPROW change.** Should be 540/241 each time if the 241-row upstream issue is independent of content.

Three logs please, one per color. Ideally: solid red, solid green, solid blue, each captured for at least 2-3 probes so we see stability.

**Excellent test — this is exactly what we needed.** Three discrete steady states, one per source color:

| Section | Source (claimed) | Repeating 3-byte pattern | Which byte is at 0xC0 |
|---|---|---|---|
| Frames 32–167 | RED | `00 C0 00` | byte 1 (middle) |
| Frames 235–439 | GREEN | `C0 00 00` | byte 0 (first) |
| Frames 506+ | BLUE | `00 00 C0` | byte 2 (last) |

Every pattern is clean and stable across multiple probes within each section. **Peak value is 0xC0 for every channel — uniform A2D saturation point, not 0xFF.** That's an analog-chain fact we now know about and can account for later.

## Byte order in memory: GRB, not BGR or RGB

If your color sequence really was R→G→B, then the byte-to-channel mapping is:

```
memory byte 0 = G
memory byte 1 = R
memory byte 2 = B
```

This is **not** the standard MIPI CSI-2 RGB888 byte order (which is R, G, B in that sequence per pixel). Two possibilities:

1. **Your color sequence was actually G→R→B** (e.g., the Wii's color picker labels things differently, or the buttons you pressed don't map to what you think). Check: did "red" on your source look red on the tap-off HDMI display, or actually green? If red looks red on the display but we're receiving the green-byte-position pattern for it, then…
2. **There's a channel swap somewhere in the chain** — most likely ElectronWarp (component Y/Pb/Pr → HDMI has a known convention; getting it wrong produces exactly this kind of single-channel swap).

Either way, the **byte order is deterministic and consistent** — we now know exactly which byte-position carries which real channel once you confirm the sequence.

## What did NOT change across the three colors

- **VPCOL=540, VPROW=241** — identical. Upstream is content-independent.
- **60-row cliff** — identical. Cliff is not color-related.
- **Pattern covers ~50% of each row with zeros on edges** — identical for all three colors.
- **Pattern phase shifts row-to-row** — same for all colors.

So **all the remaining pipeline oddities are structural, not content-dependent.** They'll persist regardless of what image is on the source. This is a really clean separation.

## What I'd suggest you verify before we go further

1. **Was the sequence actually R→G→B?** If yes, byte order is GRB and there's a channel swap upstream to track down (probably ElectronWarp). If the sequence was different, tell me what the actual order was.
2. **Does "red" on your source display as red on a separate HDMI display?** If yes, the swap is between the TC358743-to-ISC path (unlikely) or between the Wii output and the source display (happens before the splitter). If no, the Wii is outputting a different color than you think.

Once we confirm the byte order + channel mapping, we can move on with confidence — we have a **known, reliable, deterministic RGB capture path**, just with a row-count/per-row-width limit we still need to understand upstream.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 22:00:26Z)**_

**This is the cleanest dataset yet, and the results are mathematically beautiful.** Plotting the primary-color responses against the earlier orange measurement:

## The A2D chain is LINEAR, not clipping

For every test:

| Channel input | Observed output | Expected (under linear gain 0.753) |
|---|---|---|
| R=0xFF (red, white) | 0xC0 | 0xFF × 0.753 = 0xC0 ✓ |
| G=0xFF (green, white) | 0xC0 | 0xC0 ✓ |
| B=0xFF (blue, white) | 0xC0 | 0xC0 ✓ |
| R=0xFF (orange) | 0xC0 | 0xC0 ✓ |
| G=0xC0 (orange) | 0x90 | 0xC0 × 0.753 = 0x90 ✓ |
| B=0x80 (orange) | 0x60 | 0x80 × 0.753 = 0x60 ✓ |

**Every single data point fits `output = input × 0.753`.** No clipping, just a well-defined analog gain ≈ 75.3% through the component→HDMI chain (component video signal levels are inherently lower than full-scale HDMI RGB; that's the A2D stage you mentioned). Fully invertible in software if we ever want "true" RGB values.

## Memory byte order: confirmed GRB per pixel

With R→G→B source sequence verified:

```
memory[pixel * 3 + 0] = G
memory[pixel * 3 + 1] = R
memory[pixel * 3 + 2] = B
```

Every primary-color test hits exactly the predicted byte position with 0x00 on the other two — deterministic and reproducible across hundreds of frames.

(Side note on *why* GRB: either the TC358743 packs its CSI-TX this way for DT=0x24, or CSI2DC's RMS=1 byte stream permutes. Doesn't matter functionally — we remap at render time.)

## Structural issues are content-independent (good for us)

Across all 4 colors, these are **identical** to the byte:
- `VPCOL=540, VPROW=241`
- 60 rows captured out of 480
- ~50% of each row has pattern, rest zeros
- Pattern phase shifts between rows identically

So the pipeline's partial-capture behavior has **nothing to do with pixel content** — it's 100% a structural property of the TC358743/CSI/CSI2DC/ISC chain as currently configured. That means we can reason about it with pure-black source or any other test pattern; we don't need to carefully construct inputs.

## Phase 5b — I think we can call it

We now have a **fully characterized RGB888 capture path**:
- Linear A2D, invertible
- Known byte order
- Reproducible, content-independent structural quirks
- Real RGB pixel content in memory for the captured region

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 22:01:29Z)**_

Summary of where we are and where to go:

## What we proved

- **RGB888 capture is definitively working end-to-end.** Memory byte order is `[G, R, B]` per pixel. A2D chain is linear with gain ≈ 0.753. Both fully characterized.
- **Partial-capture quirks are content-independent.** 60 rows / ~50%-wide / `VPROW=241` — all identical regardless of source. That's a huge diagnostic simplification: we can reason about these without worrying about source content.

## Three paths forward, your pick

1. **Phase 6 — get pixels on the LCD.** Use the current partial capture, apply GRB → device-RGB swap + inverse A2D gain, render to Legato. You'll get a ~60-row, ~350-pixel-wide image in the middle of the LCD. Not pretty, but proves the render path works, and **any subsequent upstream fix immediately fills in more of the frame** without changing render code. Quickest win.

2. **Upstream: fix VPROW=241 and ~50%-per-row active area.** Both are almost certainly TC358743 / source-timing issues. One flash with TC358743 video-timing register dump tells us a lot. If the Wii is truly outputting 480i and TC358743 is passing fields as "p"-labeled frames, there's a mode-detection fix; if TC358743 has an active-area register too narrow, there's a config fix. This is the ceiling — getting full 480 rows of 720 active pixels.

3. **RMS=1 cliff.** Root-cause the 129,600-byte limit. Prior journal's 37 cycles suggest this is genuinely hard; could be AHB/DDR contention, internal ISC FIFO, or errata. Lowest expected ROI.

My recommendation is **(1) then (2)**: get a visible result first, then widen the capture. (3) can wait or be resolved as a side effect of (2). What do you want to do?

Plan: add a bridge-side register dump that runs right after TC358743 format detection, *before* ISC capture starts. We need:

| Register | Purpose | What we expect to see |
|---|---|---|
| `DE_WIDTH_H/V` | HDMI input active area (already read) | 720 × 480 |
| `H_SIZE, V_SIZE` | Full HDMI raster incl. blanking | ≈ 858 × 525 for 480p |
| `FH_MIN/MAX, FV_CNT` | Detected timing | ≈ 15.73 kHz, 60 Hz |
| `VI_STATUS1/3` | Interlace flag, color space | progressive |
| `HDMI_DET` | HDMI input detection mode | HDMI sync locked |
| `VI_MODE` | Color path (RGB vs DVI) | RGB |
| `CONFCTL` | CSI-TX enable + format | VBUFEN, YCBCRFMT |
| `FIFOCTL` | CSI-TX FIFO threshold | 0x0176 (=374) per current code |
| `CSI_STATUS, CSI_ERR` | CSI-TX lane health | no errors |

The critical comparison: **does the bridge think it's sending 720×480 on CSI-TX?** If yes, the narrowing is in CSI RX/CSI2DC/ISC (unlikely given prior diagnostics). If no, we find it on the bridge.

Clean. Flash this and share the log. The key signal to look for in the output:

**If the bridge reports `detected 720x480p` but CSI-TX side has narrow WC/timing** → bridge is the narrowing point. Likely a bridge config.

**If the bridge reports `720x480p` and CSI-TX looks clean (CSI_ERR=0, CSI_STATUS healthy) but CSI2DC only sees VPROW=241** → narrowing is happening on the MIPI wire or in CSI2DC. Could be a D-PHY timing issue or CSI2DC misframing short packets.

Specific values that will clinch it:

- **`raster ? × ?` (H_SIZE × V_SIZE):** for 480p this should be 858×525. If V_SIZE reads 262 or 263, the bridge is genuinely in interlaced-field mode despite the `p` flag. If V_SIZE reads 525, the bridge sees a full progressive frame — narrowing is downstream of the bridge's video-input stage.
- **`FIFOCTL`:** should be 0x0176 (374). If wrong or bouncing, CSI-TX FIFO may be underrunning.
- **`CSI_ERR`:** any non-zero bits here point at specific CSI-TX lane issues.
- **`CONFCTL.VBUFEN`:** if not set, CSI-TX isn't actually streaming the video buffer.

Flash when ready.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 22:08:30Z)**_

**Found the smoking gun.** Raster is `858 × 1050` — but standard 480p60 should be `858 × 525`. **V_TOTAL is exactly 2× what it should be.** That's the source of the 241-row delivery (which itself is ≈480/2).

Three hypotheses ranked by likelihood:

1. **The source (ElectronWarp) is outputting something other than standard 480p60.** Actual pixel clock at 858×1050×60 = 54 MHz, which is 2× the 27 MHz expected for 480p60. This could be:
   - A "doubled-vertical" mode (544p-ish, or 1080p60 truncated, or upscaler artifact)
   - 480i60 being miscounted as "progressive" by the bridge with both fields summed into VTOTAL

2. **The bridge miscounts V_SIZE.** Could be a register interpretation quirk — e.g., counting lines × 2 for interlaced detection with the "p" flag indicating scan type of each field rather than the frame.

3. **TC358743 is seeing a valid signal but its active-area (720×480) + huge blanking (1050-480=570 lines) is a legitimate but unusual mode** — some upconverters pad heavily for HDMI compliance.

Either way, **the bridge is only emitting ~240 active lines per CSI-TX frame** because it's dividing the input somehow — fields interleaved, or half-rate output because pixel clock is too fast.

Rest of the bridge data looks clean though:
- `CONFCTL=0x0003` → VBUFEN + ABUFEN, video buffer enabled ✓
- `FIFOCTL=0x0176` → our configured 374 ✓
- `CSI_ERR=0x00000000` → no CSI-TX errors ✓
- `VI_STATUS1=0x00` → no interlace flag set
- `HDMI_DET=0xC1` → MOD1+MOD0 set (full HDMI detection), V_SYNC synchronous, no errors

So the bridge's own logic thinks things are fine. The evidence of the issue is purely in **V_TOTAL=1050** and downstream lost rows.

## Things that would confirm the hypothesis

One more register read would help decide: **`FH_MIN/MAX` (0x85AA–0x85AD)** — the detected horizontal sync frequency. Standard 480p = 15.73 kHz. If we see ~31.5 kHz (×2), confirms doubled timing. If ~15.73 kHz, then V_SIZE register is bogus and the real timing is 480p standard.

Also worth a side test: **point the HDMI output into the other display (the one tapping off the splitter) and check if it reports the incoming resolution/mode**. If it says "480p" or "544p" or "1080i" — that's the actual mode the ElectronWarp is emitting and we know what we're dealing with.

## Key diagnostic: ask the secondary display

Before another flash, the simplest test: **pull up the info/display menu on the secondary HDMI display** (the one tapped off the splitter, not the bridge) and read what it reports as the incoming input mode / resolution. Every HDMI display has this — it'll say something like `720×480p 60Hz` or `1920×1080i 60Hz` or whatever ElectronWarp is actually emitting.

- If the secondary display reports **480p60** → TC358743 is wrong about V_TOTAL=1050 (bridge register quirk); signal is standard 480p and the 241-row issue must be in the bridge's CSI-TX decimating.
- If the secondary display reports **480i60** (interlaced) → ElectronWarp is outputting interlaced, TC358743's `detected 720x480p` is misleading, and we're seeing one 240-line field per CSI-TX frame. Fix: reconfigure the bridge to handle 480i, or deinterlace in software.
- If it reports something else entirely (say **540p** or **1080i**) → ElectronWarp is upconverting/transforming beyond expectations and we need a different source mode.

This one piece of info picks our next move cleanly. The current build is fine to keep running — no need to reflash for this test.

_**Agent (claude-opus-4-7 2026-05-01 22:16:28Z)**_

Good data point from the kernel driver found: `FIFO_LEVEL=374` is what the kernel uses, but its own comment explicitly warns:

> A value of 16 works with a 594Mbps data rate for 720p60 (using 2 lanes) and 1080p60 (using 4 lanes), but fails when the data rate is increased, **or a lower pixel clock is used that result in CSI reading out faster than the data is arriving**.

**That's our exact situation.** We're at 594 Mbps/lane (×2 lanes = 1188 Mbps CSI bandwidth) but source is only 480p60 RGB888 = 720 × 480 × 24 × 60 ≈ **498 Mbps total payload**. CSI-TX drains ~2.4× faster than data arrives. The FIFO perpetually underruns, and the bridge's coping mechanism is to **drop every other line**. That matches the 241/480 ≈ 50% halving exactly.

## Proposed test: lower the CSI-TX bit rate

Current: `PLL_FBD=44 → 27MHz/4 × 44 × 2 = 594 Mbps/lane`

Target: somewhere that CSI-TX rate ≈ source rate × modest overhead. Source = 498 Mbps, want CSI ≈ 600–700 Mbps total = 300–350 Mbps/lane. That's roughly half our current rate — **`PLL_FBD=22 → 297 Mbps/lane, 594 Mbps total`**.

One catch: the SAM9X75 CSI-RX's `HSFREQRANGE` setting must match the new lower rate. It's currently `csiBitRate = 0x14` (297 MHz clock-lane band). For ~150 MHz clock lane we need a different band value.

		if (IS_ERR(config_gpio)) {

			return CTRL_4_LANES;
		}
		ret = gpiod_get_value(config_gpio);
	} else {
		ret = dphy->config_8l;
	}

	dev_vdbg(&dphy->phy->dev,
		 "Booting in [%s] mode\n",
		 ret == CTRL_8_LANES ? "8L" : "4+4L");
	return ret;

#endif /* CONFIG_DWC_MIPI_TC_DPHY_GEN3 */
	return CTRL_4_LANES;
}

		return;

	iowrite32(data, dphy->dphy2_if_addr + address);
}
